case_source: (Arising out of other Class Appeal No. 36 of 2009)
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal, J:- This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 20.7.2010 passed by the learned District Judge, Mymensingh in Other Class Appeal No. 36 of 2009 reversing the order No. 18 dated 11.2.2009 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Iswargonj in other Class Suit No. 53 of 2007 rejecting the plaint should not be set aside.

2. The necessary facts for the disposal of this Rule are as follows:

The opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 53 of 2007 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Iswargonj for setting-aside the judgment and decree dated 28.01.1981 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Iswargonj stating, inter-alia, that Koilash Chandra Roy was originally owner of .33 acres of land in total, who died leaving two sons named Kumud Chandra Roy and Promode Chandra Roy. By way of amicable partition the suit properties fell on the Saham of Kumud Chandra Roy, who left for India after 1947. Promote Chandra Roy got the land of plot No. 1492 and he appointed one Monoranjan Roy verbally to look after the properties. Promode Chandra Roy also left for India and consequently, the entire properties of plot No. 1492 had been enlisted as enemy property by operation of law. Monoranjan Roy Poddar possessed the properties peacefully for more than 40 years. The father of defendant No. 1 instituted other class Suit No. 292 of 79 in the Court of Munsif, Iswarganj on the basis of a Bainapatra and obtained an exparte decree by suppressing the summons. The averments made in the plaint of the Other Class Suit No. 292 of 1979 are false and without any legal basis No summon of the suit was served upon the defendants. The plaintiff came to know about the exparte decree on 11.2.07 for the first time and after having obtained the certified copy of that decree on 13.3.07 instituted the suit for the relief stated above.

3. The defendant Nos. 1 & 2 contested the suit by filing two separate written statements denying the material allegations of the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, the suit is barred by limitation and the principles of res-judicata. The case of the defendant No.1 in short, is that Promode Chandra Roy proposed to transfer the schedule-2 properties of the plaint to Digendra Chandra Sarker (father of the defendant No. 1) on the first part of 1956 and his father having agreed to purchase and negotiated the price which was ultimately fixed at Tk. 1,500/- and accordingly Promode Chandra Roy after receiving the entire money from the father of the defendant No. 1 executed a baina patra in favour of his father and handed over possession of the properties with a condition that deed will be executed & registered after obtaining the income tax clearance certificate by the seller. The father of defendant No. 1 subsequently instituted other class Suit No. 292 of 79 in the Court of the then Munsif, Iswarganj on the basis of that bainapatra and obtained an exparte decree on 28.1.81. The S.D.O. Sadar (North), Mymenshingh filed a Misc. Case being No. 571/81 for setting aside the exparte decree which was rejected on 19.1.86. A.D.C. (Revenue) also filed another Misc. Case being No. 100/82 which was dismissed on 15.5.83. One Abdul Hye also Sled O.C. Suit No. 98/81 on the strength of obtaining lease from Government for setting aside the exparte decree, but ultimately the suit was dismissed on 31.8.82 and an appeal being No. 299/83 was preferred against the dismissal order but it was also dismissed on 18.5.86. The father of defendant No. 1 applied for the release of the suit properties to the A.D. C. (Revenue) and mutated his name in the record of rights on 8.9,87. He also gifted some properties to his nephew who also mutated his name and both of them have been paying rents to the Government. The defendant No. 1 being the successor on the death of his father transferred some properties to others and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The case of the defendant No. 2 is that the entire properties of plot Nos. 1492 & 1493 have been enlisted as enemy properties and his father took lease of the properties from the Government and thereafter, defendant No. 2 obtained lease and has been possessing the properties peacefully. The decree was obtained in Other Class Suit No. 292 of 79 by suppressing summons and practicing fraud upon the Court and as such the same is liable to be set-aside.

5. After filing written statement the defendant No. 1 on 06.01.2009 filed an application under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code for rejection of plaint stating, inter-alia, that the defendant No.1 got the land by inheritance from his late father Digendra. Chandra Sarker, who was the owner of the land by purchase, while Digendra Chandra Sarker was owing and possessing the land the Government claimed the land as vested property and as such Digendra Chandra Sarker filed Title Suit No. 292 of 1979 and obtained an ex-parte decree on 28.01.1981 and thereafter, the then Sub Divisional officer, Sadar North, Mymensingh filed other class suit No. 571 of 1981 in the Court of Munsif, 2nd Court, Mymensingh for setting-aside the said ex-parte decree. The said suit was subsequently, transferred to the Court of the then Munsif, Iswargonj for disposal, who however, dismissed the suit on 19.01.1986. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Mymensingh on behalf of the Government filed. Miscellaneous case No. 100 of 1982 which was rejected on 15.05.1983. One Abdul Hye Ansar Commander took the land lease from the vested property authority under. the Government and filed other class suit No. 98 of 1981 for setting-aside the ex-parte decree passed in the said other class suit No. 292 of 1979. The said other class suit No. 98 of 1981 was dismissed on 31.08.1982 and the plaintiff filed Other Class Appeal in the Court of District Judge, Mymensingh which was dismissed on 18:4.86. The predecessor of the defendant No. 1 filed an application to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Mymenshingh for releasing the property from the list of vested property and ultimately, the property has been released from the list of vested property and thereafter, the suit property was mutated in the name of the father of defendant No. 1, vide latter No. 3418(4) S. A. T. and Khatian No. 1034 has been opened in the name of the father of the defendant No. 1 and as such, the suit is barred by law of resjudicata.

6. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Iswargonj upon hearing the parties by order No. 18 dated 11.02.2009 allowed the application under order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure holding that the present plaintiff as defendant after being unsuccessful in earlier suit filed the instant suit over the self same matter and between the self same parties and as such, the suit is plainly barred by law of resjudicata.

7. Feeling aggrieved thereby the Deputy Commissioner, Mymensingh on behalf of the Government as appellant preferred Other Class Appeal No. 36 of 2009 in the Court of learned District Judge, Mymensingh who upon hearing the appeal by the impugned judgment and order dated 20.7.2010 allowed the appeal and set-aside the order No. 18 dated 11.2.2009 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Iswarganj in Other Class Suit No. 53 of 2007 rejecting the plaint and the instant Revisional application is directed against that judgment and order.

8. Mr. Md. Abdul Haque, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the appellate Court below without considering the application for rejection of the plaint and the previous cases held in between the parties and the judgment passed in those cases regarding the same subject matter erroneously reversed the judgment and order of the trial Court and thereby committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice.He next in the course of argument upon placing the relevant materials on record submits that the appellate Court below ought to have considered that the decree passed in other class suit No. 292 of 1979 on 28.01.1981 was challenged by the Government by filing other class suit No. 571 of 1981 in the Court of the then Munsif, 2nd Court, Mymensingh which was subsequently renumbered on transfer as other class Suit No. 273 of 1984 and ultimately, the said suit was dismissed and thereafter, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Mymensingh filed Miscellaneous case No. 100 of 1982 which was rejected on 15.02.1983 as such the Government is not legally entitled to file the present suit for same relief against the same subject matter but the appellate Court below without considering this aspect of the case most illegally allowed the appeal and set-aside the order of the trial court thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice.

9. Mr. Md. Abdul Haque, further submits that the appellate Court below having failed to understand that the plaintiff-opposite party of the other class suit No. 53 of 2007 in a malafide manner suppressed the facts that the Government became unsuccessful in challenging the decree passed in other class Suit No. 292 of 1979 by filing other class suit No. 571 of 1981 and Miscellaneous case No. 100 of 1982 respectively. He finally submits that the Government released the property from the fist of vested property infavour of the predecessor of the present defendant No. 1 and the Government also took rent from the defendant-petitioner and thus, the Government has no locus-standi to file the suit and the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation and resjudicata as well and as such, the impugned Judgment and order of the appellate Court caused a failure of justice.

10. Mr. Arobinda Kumar Roy, the learned Assistant Attorney General, on the other hand, appearing for the Government represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Mymensingh by filing counter affidavit opposes the Rule. He submits that the trial Court below having failed to consider that it is admitted in the plaint of Tile Suit No. 292 of 1979 that the suit property has been enlisted as vested property but in the said suit Digendra did not make any prayer to the effect that enlistment of the suit property in the V.P. list is void, illegal etc. and therefore, the suit was not maintainable. He further submits that Court of appeal below as last Court of fact in the facts and circumstance of the case rightly held that there is no legal scope to reject the plaint unless the plaint itself shows the want of cause of action for the suit or the suit being barred by any law but in the instant case the trial Court below wrongly by invoking the provision of Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure has rejected the plaint in spite of the fact that neither in the plaint contained any statement to hold apparently that the plaint is liable to be rejected nor the suit is barred by any law. Mr. Roy, finally submits that the dismissal of an application filed under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot operate bar in instituting a fresh suit for setting aside an exparte decree as per the provision of law but the trial court below upon misconception of law erroneously rejected the plaint which cannot be sustained in law and as such, the rule is liable to be discharged. Mr. Arobinda Kumar Roy, the learned Assistant Attorney General to fortify his argument has relied on the decision reported in 10 BLC (AD) 8 and 44 DLR (AD) 242.

11. Mr. Probir Neogi and Mr. Khijir Ahmed, the learned Advocates appearing for the opposite party No. 2 support the impugned judgment and order of the Court of appeal below, which were according to them, just, correct and proper. Mr. Probir Neogi in the course of his argument after placing the counter affidavit dated 12.1.2012 filed on behalf of the opposite party No. 2 submits that the application filed by the defendant petitioner under Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code for rejection of the plaint was misconceived one inasmuch as the opposite party No. 1, Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Mymensingh as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 53 of 2007 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, lswargonj impleading the defendant petitioner herein praying for setting-aside the exparte decree dated 28.01.1981 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, lswargonj in Other Class Suit No. 292 of 1979 on the allegation that the said exparte decree was obtained on practicing fraud upon the Court without serving notice upon the defendants and in that view of the matter there is no legal scope to reject the plaint on the ground that the Suit is barred by resjudicata. Mr. Probir Neogi further submits that whether the suit is barred by resjudicata or not, is a matter to be decided at the time of trial, as raised by the defendants, and the same cannot be decided from a reading of the plaint and in the instant case the Court of appeal below on assigning sound reason rightly reversed the order No. 18 dated 11.2.2009 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Iswargonj in Other Class Suit No. 53 of 2007 rejecting the plaint on the ground of res-judicata. He adds that the maintainability of the suit on the ground of res-judicata can very well be framed' s an issue in the suit.

12. Mr. Probir Neogi also submits that it is apparent from the materials on record that the trial Court below in deciding an application under order VII, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure traveled beyond the pleadings of the plaint and consequently, the Court of appeal below rightly set-aside the order of the trial Court dated 11.2.2009. Mr. Probir Neogi in support of his argument has relied on the decisions reported in 57 DLR (AD) l8, 53 DLR (AD) 62 and 52 DLR (AD) 49.

13. Mr. Khijir Ahmed also appearing for the opposite party No. 2 upon relying on a decision reported in 13 BLD (AD) 217 submits that the plea about the question of limitation and resjudicata are mixed question of law and fact which need to be decided at the time of trial, as raised by the defendants and the same cannot be decided from a reading of the plaint.

14. I have perused the record and considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for both the sides and the learned Assistant Attorney General.

15. It appears that the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 53 of 2007 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Iswargonj for setting-aside the ex-pane decree dated 28.01.1981 on the allegation that the said ex-parte decree was obtained on practicing fraud upon the Court. After filing written statement the petitioner as defendant No. 1 on 06.012009 filed an application under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code for rejection of plaint stating, inter-alia, that the defendant No. 1 got the land by inheritance from his late father Digendra Chandra Sarker who was the owner of the land by purchase, while Digendra Chandra Sarker as owner was in possession of the land the Government claimed the land as vested property as such Digendra Chandra Sarker filed Title Suit No. 292 of 1979 and got a ex-partee decree on 28,01.1981. Thereafter, the then Sub-divisional officer, sadar (North) Mymensingh for setting aside the decree filed other class suit No. 571 of 1981 in the Court of Munsif, 2nd Court, Mymensingh, subsequently the said suit was transferred to the Court of Munsif Iswargonj, who dismissed the same on 19.01.1986. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Mymensingh on behalf of the Government filed Miscellaneous case No. 100 of 1982 which was rejected on 15.05.1983. One Abdul Hye Ansar Commander took the land lease from the vested property department and filed other class suit No. 98 of 1981 for setting aside the decree passed in other class suit No. 292 of 1979. The other class suit No. 98 of 1981 was dismissed on 31.08.1982 and than filed other class Appeal in the Court of District Judge, Mymensingh which was ultimately dismissed on 18.4.86. The predecessor of the defendant No. 1 filed an application to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Mymenshingh for releasing the property from the vested property and eventually, the said property was released from the list of vested property and subsequently, the property was mutated in the name of the father of the defendant no.1 vide order issued in latter No. 3418(4) S. A. T. and Khatian No. 1034 has been opened in the name of the father of the defendant No. 1 and hence, the suit is barred by law of resjudicata.

16. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Iswargonj, however, by his order No. 18 dated 11.2.2009 rejected the plaint holding that the Government as plaintiff earlier over the self-same subject matter after being unsuccessful in other class suit No. 571 of 1984 and Miscellaneous Case No. 100 of 1982 as well filed the instant Suit and as such the suit is plainly barred by law of resjudicata. The Court of appeal below in its turn relying on the decision reported in 57 DLR (AD) 18 set-aside the order of the trial Court.

17. Now, the question for consideration is, whether the Court of appeal below was justified in setting-aside the order of the trial Court holding that the learned Assistant Judge appears to have passed the order of rejection of plaint illegally by wrongly invoking the provision of order VII, Rule 11 C.P.C.

18. In order to resolve this dispute, I have examined the averments of the plaint. It appears that the opposite party' No. 1, Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Mymensingh as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 53 of 2007 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Iswargonj impleading the defendant petitioner herein for Setting-aside the exparte decree dated 28.01.1981 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Iswargonj in Other Class Suit No. 292 of 1979 on the allegation that the said exparte decree was obtained on practicing fraud upon the Court without serving notice upon the defendants.

19. It is now well settled that in considering an application filed under order 7, Rule 11 of the Code the Court cannot travel beyond the averments made by the plaintiff in his plaint Mr. Md. Abdul Haque, the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioners did not dispute this proposition of law rather at the time of arguing on this point he fully agreed with the learned Advocates for the plaintiff-opposite parties.

<u>20. From a reading of the averments made by the plaintiff in his plaint and the reliefs claimed in the suit, I am of the opinion that contents of the plaint do disclose cause of action for filing the suit Exparte decree dated 28.01.1981 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Iswargonj in Other Class Suit No. 292 of 1979 was obtained on practicing fraud upon the Court without serving notice upon the defendants cannot be decided from a reading of the plaint without taking evidence at the time of trial.</u>

<u>21. On a perusal of the averments of the plaint, I find nothing in the plaint to suggest that the suit is impliedly barred by any law rather the contents of the plaint do disclose cause of action against the defendants. Therefore, the Court of appeal below committed no illegality in holding that the learned Assistant Judge appears to have passed the order of rejection of plaint illegally by wrongly invoking the provision of order VII, Rule 11 C.P.C. Moreover, the dismissal of an application filed under order IX rule 13 of the C.P.C. also cannot operate as a bar in instituting a fresh suit for setting aside the exparte decree.</u>

22. Now, it remains for me to consider the real question in this case, whether the trial Court below committed any illegality in holding that the Government as plaintiff earlier over the self same issue after being unsuccessful in other class suit No. 571 of 1984 and Miscellaneous Case Not 00 of 1982 as well filed the instant Suit and as such the instant suit is impliedly barred by law of resjudicata.

23. 1n deciding this point, I must quote hereunder few lines of the cited cases for having a better view of the dispute in question.

24. In the case of Sreemati Pushpa Rani Das. vs. A.K.M. Habibur Rahman and others reported in 13 BLD (AD) 217, it has been held that:

"Whether the suit is barred by resjudicata or not is matter to be decided at the time of trial, as raised by the defendants, and the same cannot be decided from a reading of the plaint. The maintainability of the suit on the ground of resjudicata can very well be framed as an issue in the suit."

25. In the case of Mahbubul Haque vs. Md. A. Kader Munshi reported in 52 DLR (AD) 49, it has been held that:

"Plaintiff - respondents having alleged that fraud was practiced by the defendant-petitioner upon the plaintiff as well as the Court in the earlier suit by producing forged documents he cannot be non-suited at the threshold since the question of resjudicata and limitation are mixed question of law and fact. High Court Division relied on the decision in the case of Sreemati Pushpa Rani Das vs. AKM Habibur Rahman & ors reported in 13 BLD (AD) 217 in which it has been held that question of resjudicata cannot be decided from a reading of the plaint and should be decided at the time of trial. The High Court Division also held relying on another decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Shahabuddin vs. Habibur Rahman reported in 50 DLR (AD) 99 that question of limitation is a mixed question of law and fact which can be decided at the time of trial on taking evidence. The learned Advocate for the petitioner could not show that the High Court Division committed any illegality in relying upon those decisions and holding that the questions of limitation and resjudicata raised in the application under order 7 rule 11(d) of the Code for rejecting the plaint of the present suit, are mixed questions of law and fact which need thorough investigation on adequate evidence for arriving at a correct decision on framing specific issues by the trial Court. Since the petitioner would get a chance to agitate the questions at the time of trial of the suit the petition merits no consideration."

26. In the case of Abul Khair vs. Pubali Bank reported M 53 DLR (AD) 62, it has been held that:

"Where in a suit an application under Order 7 rule 11 is filed for rejecting the plaint on the ground that the averments made in the plaint do not disclose a cause of action for the suit the Court is not called upon to decide the suit on merit on taking evidence as submitted by the learned Advocate. It is only the averments made in the plaint are to be considered to come to a finding as to whether those disclose a cause of action and the Court while deciding such application is not permitted in law to travel beyond the averments made in the plaint. The High Court Division in the instant case on consideration of averments made in the plaint found that the plaint does not disclose any cause of action and for such finding we do not find and infirmity in the impugned judgment and order."

27. In the case of Abdul Malek Sawdagar vs. Mahbubey Alam reported in 57 DLR (AD) 18, it has been held that:

"The defendant has alleged that the suit from its own averment appears to be barred under section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance. While considering the application under order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Court cannot take into account materials beyond the plaint to declare the case of the plaintiff as frivolous and vexatious and the Court is not required to take into consideration the defence set up by the defendant in his written statement or written objection. The question as to whether the plaint is liable to be rejected being barred by law must be apparent from the statement made in the plaint itself and not from the written statement or any other material other than that has been put in the plaint. Thus this provision applies when it appears from the statement in the plaint that suit is barred by any law either due to limitation, res-judicata or barred by law providing ouster of the jurisdiction of the Court."

<u>28. From the above, it transpires that the question of resjudicata and limitation are mixed question of law and facts which need thorough investigation on adequate evidence for arriving at a correct decision on framing specific issues by the trial Court and in the instant case the petitioner should get a chance to agitate those questions at the time of trial of the suit. My view is therefore that in the facts and circumstance of the case the trial Court below in deciding an application under Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code most erroneously arrived at a finding that the suit is barred by law of resjudicata.</u>

29. The Court must apply its mind to the case of the plaintiff as set out in the plaint alone in deciding an application under Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code. In this case the trial Court below committed a serious error in taking into consideration the application filed by the defendant-petitioners, which resulted in the failure of justice and consequently, the Court of appeal below rightly interfered with the findings of the trial Court below. The findings, of the Court of appeal below are based on proper appreciation of facts and law and those suffer from no error of law or of procedure affecting the merit of the case. No interference is, therefore, called for.

30. By the way, it may be observed that the points raised in the application under Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code by the defendant-petitioner for rejection of the plaint appears to be based on bundle of facts, beyond the averments of the plaint which can be decided only at the trial on taking evidence.

31. For the reasons stated above, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. Since the suit has been dragging over a period of 5 years, the trial Court concerned is directed to proceed with the suit expeditiously.

32. Let a copy of this judgment along with the lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

lawyer:

parties:
Md. Abdul khaleque
Vs.
Abed Ali Munshi being dead his heirs:
1. Md. Arab Ali and others
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal, J: This Civil Revision has been remanded to this bench by their Lordships of the Appellate Division after setting-aside the judgment and order dated 17.11.2009 passed by a Single Bench of this Court vide order dated 17.11.2011 passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 279 of 2010.

2. By this Rule opposite party Nos.1-13 were called upon to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14.02.2004 (decree signed on 22.02.2004) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.205 of 2001 affirming those dated 26.02.2001 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.15 of 2000 should not be set-aside.

3. The relevant facts leading to the filing of this Revisional application are as follows:

4. The petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.15 of 2000 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka against the opposite parties for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land by removing all structure thereon along with further declaration that the judgment and decree dated 24.8.1995 (decree signed on 7.9.1995) passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.217 of 1992 is false, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff petitioner. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that one Asker Matbor originally belonged to the suit land along with other land, who died leaving behind his heirs Asraf Ali, Mir Box, Yeasin, A. Karim, Abed Ali Munshi and Fazal Karim. Later on, Yeasin died leaving behind his heirs namely Naziruddin, Sahajuddin, Majaruddin, two daughters namely, Alimon and Karimon and wife Malekjan; that the said heirs of Asker Matbor transferred their share to the plaintiff by executing registered deeds and handed over possession of the suit land to the plaintiff and the plaintiff after getting possession developed the suit land by constructing a tin shed house; that on 9.02.99 the defendant No. 2, Ahad Ali forcibly dispossessed the caretaker of the plaintiff from the suit land. The further case of the plaintiff-petitioner is that the defendant No.2 earlier instituted a suit being Title Suit No.217 of 1992 for permanent injunction in respect of the suit land against the plaintiff and others but due to his illness the plaintiff-petitioner became unsuccessful in the said Title Suit No.217 of 1992.

5. The defendant No.2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying most of the allegations made in the plaint stating, inter-alia, that the suit is defective and not maintainable in its present form and manner inasmuch as the suit is barred by law of limitation. The defendant's case is that the suit land including the other lands of the disputed holding originally belonged to C.S. recorded tenant Ashkor Ali Matbor. After the death of Ashkor Ali Matbor his legal heirs inherited the land of Ashkor Ali and they sold 87 decimals of land to Malekjan Bibi, though they had legal right to transfer only 40 decimals of land. Another son Mir Box sold 7 decimals of land to his brother Asraf Ali and in this way Ashraf Ali got 14 decimals of land and after his death his heirs transferred their share in favour of the defendant Nos.1-5 and also handed over possession. In this way the defendants got 8½ decimals of land and subsequent R.S. record has been prepared by their names. The plaintiff had no right, title and possession in the suit property and as such the story of dispossession from the suit land is false and without any basis. The plaintiff with ill motive filed the suit stating false statement which is liable to be set aside.

6. The learned Assistant Judge, Dhaka on the pleadings of the parties framed the following issues for determination:-

(i) Whether the suit is maintainable in its present form and manner?

(ii) Whether the plaintiff has got title in the suit land?

(iii) Whether the plaintiff was dispossessed from the suit land?

(iv) Whether decree in question was fraudulent?

(v) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get reliefs, as prayed for?

7. At the trial the plaintiff side examined seven witnesses while the defendant side did not examine any single witness to prove their cases.

8. The trial Court below upon hearing the parties and on considering the materials on record by its judgment and decree dated 26.02.2001 dismissed the suit mainly on two counts; (i) the plaintiff could not prove that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.217 of 1992 was fraudulent, collusive and not acted upon and (ii) the plaintiff having been failed to prove his possession and dispossession over the suit land.

9. The unsuccessful plaintiff, thereafter, preferred Title Appeal No.205 of 2001 to the Court of District Judge, Dhaka against the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.15 of 2000. Eventually, the said appeal was transmitted to the Court of Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka for hearing and disposal. The Court of appeal below by its judgment and decree dated 14.02.2004 (decree signed on 22.02.2004) dismissed the appeal and affirmed the decision of the trial Court below.

10. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 14.02.2004 the present plaintiff-appellant-petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

11. Mr. Zainul Abedin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in the course of his argument after placing the judgments of two Courts below, deposition of PWs. and other materials on record submits that the judgments of both Courts below are not based on proper appreciation of the evidence on record and as such the impugned judgment as well as judgment of the trial Court below are liable to be set aside. He further submits that both the Courts below having failed to consider that the plaintiff-petitioner purchased the suit property from the heirs of original C.S. recorded tenant Ashker Matbor through registered deed No. 5449 dated 6.02.1979 executed by Malekjan Bibi, deed No.3416 dated 6.02.1979 executed by Hayem, son of late Abdul Karim and grandson of late Askar Matbor, deed No.5501 dated 6.02.1979 executed by Sahajuddin and Samser Ali and Karimunnessa heirs of late Yeasin, deed No.5502 dated 6.02.1979 executed by Abdul Hayem, the only heir of late Abdul Karim. The learned Advocate further submits that both the Courts below without discussing anything about the material exhibits of the plaintiff namely; Ext.1-7(Uma) (title deed, via deed) and oral evidence of P.Ws. most illegally dismissed the suit on the findings that the plaintiff failed to prove that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.217 of 1992 was fraudulent, collusive and not acted upon and also failed to prove his possession and dispossession of the suit land. Mr. Zainul Abedin further argues that both the Courts below failed to consider that the earlier Title Suit No.217 of 1992 being a suit for permanent injunction and the present suit filed by the plaintiff against the defendant-opposite parties for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession along with further declaration that the judgment and decree dated 24.4.1995 passed in title suit No. 217 of 1992 is false fraudulent and not binding upon the petitioner and the plaintiff-petitioner in order to prove his case exhibited a series of registered documents namely; Ext.1-7(Uma) series. The learned Advocate finally submits that the judgments of two Courts below are based on total misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record and as such the same are liable to be set aside.

12. Mr. Zainul Abedin, the learned Advocate to fortify his submission has cited a number of decisions namely, the decisions reported in 17 DLR(AD) 162, 48 DLR(AD) 160 and 51 DLR 435.

13. Mr. Mohammad Ali Zinnah, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.11, on the other hand, by filing counter affidavit opposes the Rule. He submits that both the courts below on due consideration of the entire materials on record rightly arrived at a concurrent findings that the contesting defendant No.2, Ahad Ali along with other defendant Nos.1,3 and 4 instituted Title Suit No.217 of 1992 praying a decree for permanent injunction long before filing of the present suit against the present plaintiff-petitioner Abdul Khaleque and some others in respect of the suit land and said suit was decreed on contest and thereafter, the present petitioner filed Misc. Case No.52 of 1995 under Order IX, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.217 of 1992, the said Misc. Case was rejected vide judgment and order dated 10.3.1999 and thereafter the defendants including the present plaintiff-petitioner did not take any step against the said judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge in Title Suit No.217 of 1992 and consequently, a valid decree passed by a competent Court on contest against the defendants including the plaintiff-petitioner stands and is binding on him and as such question of possession and forcibly dispossession of the present plaintiff Abdul Khaleque from the suit land by the defendants does not arise at all. Mr. Zinnah further submits that the grievance of Mr. Zainul Abedin that the trial Court below without considering the evidence adduced and produced by the plaintiff-petitioner dismissed the suit appears to be incorrect inasmuch as it is apparent from the judgment of the trial Court below that the trial Court below on due consideration of the entire evidence and materials on record both oral and documentary arrived at a finding that the plaintiff miserably failed to prove his right, title and possession as well as dispossession of the suit property.

14. The learned Advocate further submits that the earlier suit being Title Suit No.217 of 1992 was decreed on contest wherein the present plaintiff-petitioner was defendant No.7 and after being unsuccessful in the said title suit, the said defendant as petitioner filed Misc. Case No.52 of 1995 under Order IX, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the judgment and decree and ultimately, the said Misc. case was also dismissed on contest. Against the judgment passed in Misc. Case No.52 of 1995 the present plaintiff-petitioner did not prefer any revision or appeal before the Higher Court and as such the present suit filed by the plaintiff keeping alive the judgment and decree of the self same property passed by a competent civil Court is not tenable in law. Mr. Zinnah, the learned Advocate to strengthen his argument has relied on a decision reported in 24 BLD(AD) 163.

15. Now, to effectively deal with the contentions raised by the learned Advocates for the respective parties before me, it would be convenient for me to decide first of all whether the judgments of two Courts below based on misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record or the same is perverse being contrary to law and materials on record.

<u>16. At the trial, the plaintiff-petitioner to prove his case examined as many as 7(seven) witnesses and exhibited a number of registered deeds. The trial Court below on consideration of the materials on record dismissed the suit mainly on two counts; (i) the plaintiff having been failed to prove that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.217 of 1992 was fraudulent, collusive and not acted upon and (ii) the plaintiff having been failed to prove his possession and dispossession of the suit land. It is found that the trial Court below in its judgment categorically discussed the evidence of PW-1, PW-2, PW-3, PW-4, PW-5, PW-6 and PW-7. The trial Court below on perusal of the exhibited documents namely Ext.7(Ka) to 7(Uma) and arrived at a finding that the land as described in the deeds are not inconsistent with the land as described in the schedule of the plaint. Therefore, I am unable to see eye to eye to such submission of Mr. Zainul Abedin that the Courts below without discussing any evidence of the plaintiff-petitioner mechanically dismissed the suit.</u>

17. It is also found that both the Courts below on assessment of the entire evidences on record held that the present plaintiff-petitioner filed Misc. Case No.52 of 1995 under Order IX, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.217 of 1992. The said Misc. Case was rejected vide judgment and order dated 10.3.1999 against which the plaintiff-petitioner did not prefer any appeal. It is also found that the present plaintiff-petitioner as defendant No.7 entered appearance in the earlier Title Suit No.217 of 1992 and filed written statement and also cross-examined to the PW-1 but in spite of such fact he filed Misc. Case under Order IX, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.217 of 1992.

<u>18. The Court of appeal below as last Court of fact on due consideration of the materials on record dismissed the appeal stating that "I am of the opinion that the aforesaid decree of permanent injunction is still alive, the present plaintiff has no legal right and scope to file the present suit praying for decree of recovery of khas possession. I am also of the opinion that as because the present plaintiff did not prefer any appeal or civil revision case challenging the judgment and decree dated 24.8.95 of Title Suit No.217 of 1992, his present suit praying for setting aside the said judgment and decree is not tenable in law."</u>

19. In the case of Moulana Serajul Haque Vs. Md. Saifullah reported in 24 BLD(AD) 163, it has been held that: as follows:

"It may be pointed out here that the suit land of Title Suit No.90 of 1986 and the present suit are the same. Thus it appears that so long a valid decree passed by a competent Court on contest against the defendant Md. Safiuddin stands the same is binding on him who is present plaintiff of Title Suit No.93 of 1985."

20. Admittedly, in this case the opposite party No. 11 herein and others earlier instituted a suit being Title suit No. 217 of 92 for permanent injection over the self-same suit land which was decreed in favour of them and against which the present defendant petitioner filed Misc. Case No. 52 of 95 and the said Misc. Case was rejected by order dated 10.3.1999. The defendant -petitioner against the said order of Misc. case did not file any appeal or civil revision. I, therefore, find there is a good deal of substance in the contentions raised by Mr. Mohammad Ali Zinnah that so long a valid decree passed by a competent Court on contest against the defendant-petitioner, Md. Abdul Khaleque stands, the same is binding on him.

21. On a reading of the impugned judgment of the Court of appeal below together with the above quoted decision of our Apex Court vis-a-vis the admitted facts of the case, I do not find any reason to differ with the above quoted observation of the Court of appeal below.

22. In the given facts and circumstances of the case, Mr. Zainul Abedin is not correct in submitting that both the Courts below having failed to consider that the earlier Title Suit No.217 of 1992 being a suit for permanent injunction and the present suit filed by the plaintiff against the defendant-opposite parties for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession along with further declaration that the judgment and decree dated 24.4.1995 passed in title suit No. 217 of 1992 is false, fraudulent and not binding upon the petitioner is well maintainable.

23. Mr. Zainul Abedin, however, upon placing the materials on record could not show any error of law or infirmity in the impugned judgments or findings of the courts below are either arbitrary or fanciful or findings of the Courts below are product of misreading and non considering the evidence on record. The decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner are distinguishable on facts. After considering the submission of Mr. Zainul Abedin, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, I am not persuaded that the findings require interference by this Court. The concurrent findings are based on relevant evidence on record and those suffer from no error of law or of procedure affecting the merit of the case.

24. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

25. Let a copy of this judgment be sent down at once.

End.

case_source: (From Judgment and order dated o4. 11. 1999 passed by the Court Division in Appeal from Original Decree (FA.) probate No. 246 of 1999)
full_judgment:
Abu Sayeed Ahammed, J.: This appeal is at the instance of the contesting defendant and is directed against the impugned judgment and order dated 04.11.1999 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in the First Appeal (Probate) No. 246 of 1996, allowing the appeal on compromise and granting probate upon the disputed will and thereby setting aside the judgment and order dated 20.05.1996 passed by the Additional District Judge, 1st court, Barisal in Probate Case No. 02 of 1992, refusing to grant probate of the last will of Trailakha Nath Roy made in favour of the respondent No. 1 Swarashati Roy wife of him.

2. Facts in this case, in short, are that Trailakha Nath Roy was the husband of the respondent No. 1 Swarashati Roy. Swarashati Roy and her son Bolai Roy used to look after the property of the said testator, Trailakha Nath Roy during his old age till his death. Trailakha Nath Roy made a will on 25.5.1990 and he died on 12.01.1991. Swarashati Roy was named as the executrix in the said will, Swarshati Roy and her son Bolai Roy filed Probate Case No. 2 of 1992 in the Court of the District Delegate Judge who is also the Additional District Judge, Barisal who refused to grant probate by his judgment and order dated 20.05.1996 upon the said will on contest by the parties in that case.

3. Against the said judgment and order of the District Delegate Judge First Appeal No. 246 of 1996 was filed, before the High Court Division by the present appellant who was contesting in the said Probate Case. In the High Court Division, the parties filed a compromise petition in the said First Appeal. And the Court Division granted the probate as was prayed for, by the compromise petition and in the terms of the compromise. Its noticed that the appellant herein contested in the probate case in the original Court contending inter alia that the will itself was not genuine and it was a forged and fabricated one created by the respondent No. 1. Swarashati Roy, respondent No. 1 and her son Bolai Roy, the respondent no. 2 after death of the said testator of the will. Upon healing the parties the trial court refused granting of probate by its judgment and order dated 04.11.1999. But in the compromise petition before the High Court Division on 18.11.1999 it was stated that the parties being relatives, on the advice of their common relatives and according to the instruction of their common well wishers the parties have compromised the matter outside the court and the parties would not contest the appeal before the High Court Division. In the compromise petition prayer was made to allow the appeal and to grant probate upon the said will and accordingly the compromise petition was accepted by the High Court Division and the First Appeal (Probate) No. 246 of 1996 was allowed on 30.11.1999 making the terms and conditions of the compromise petition as part of the judgment and order and thereby it set aside the judgment and order of the trial court who granted by the High Court Division in favour of said Swarashati Roy, the executrix of the will, respondent No.1.

4. Against that judgment and order of the High Court Division granting Probate on compromise said Kanai Lal Roy has filed the leave petition No. 267 of 2000 and obtained the order of granting leave in this appeal to consider the grievance of the petitioner whether the High Court Division has jurisdiction to grant the Probate merely on the consent of the parties without the will being proved in accordance with law.

5. It is noticed that the appellant filed an application before the High Court Division for vacating the order of granting probate on compromise stating inter alia that in filing the petition of compromise in the High Court Division, fraud was practiced upon him and also it has been alleged that the lawyer of Kanai Lal, the appellant, Mr. M.K. Rahman did not take his consent in submitting the compromise petition. The High Court Division did not lend any importance to the said application and the learned Judges of the High Court Division finding inter alia that the allegation of fraud was concocted one, rejected the application for vacating the order of granting the probate and the High Court Division further found that the parties voluntarily consented to the terms and conditions of the compromise petition and the High Court Division did not allow the allegation of restoration of the appeal to its file and number upon vacating its earlier order dated 9.11.1999 granting probate.

<u>6. We have heard the learned Counsels of both parties and upon considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division, we are of the view is that although there is a will but unless and until it is proved in accordance with law, on the face of objection raised by any interested party (herein the appellant) a Probate cannot be granted on compromise and it is not permitted by law.</u>

<u>7. For the reasons and discussions made above, we find merits in the appeal and accordingly the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is set aside and order of granting probate on compromise is set aside and it is cancelled. The probate case, however, is sent back to the original court, for hearing the same afresh in accordance with law by giving opportunity to the concerned party to produce the will itself in question and prove it by adducing evidence.</u>

<u>No order as to costs.</u>

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Masood R. Sobhan with Ms. Fatema S. Chowdhury and Mr. A.F.M. Saiful Karim, Advocates ------ For the Petitioners (in both the Rules)

parties:

Bangladesh Represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and others (In Writ Petition No. 11905 of 2015)
With
Rubaiya Binta Rafiq and others
Vs.
Bangladesh Represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and others (In Writ Petition No. 11582 of 2015)
full_judgment:
Quamrul Islam Siddique, J: Both the Writ Petition Nos. 11905 of 2015 and 11582 of 2015 are heard together and are being disposed of by this common judgment as they do involve common question of law and facts.

2. In Writ Petition No. 11905 of 2015, Rule Nisi was issued in the following terms:

"Let a Rule Nisi issue calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the respondents shall not be directed to give registration number to the petitioners including other students of Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS) admitted in different Private Dental Colleges of Bangladesh securing above the cut-off mark 105 out of 200 in the admission test and having other requisite educational qualifications and /or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. In Writ Petition No. 11582 of 2015, Rule Nisi was issued in the following terms:

"Let a Rule Nisi issue calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the respondents shall not be directed to give registration number to the petitioners including other students of Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BIDS) admitted in different Private Dental Colleges of Bangladesh securing above the cut-off mark 105 out of 200 in the admission test and having other requisite educational qualifications and /or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

4. At the time of issuance of the Rules, the respondents were directed to allow the petitioners including the other students of Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BIDS) admitted in different Private Dental Colleges of Bangladesh who had secured above the cut-off mark 105 out of 200 in the admission test and having other requisite educational qualification to appear at their yearly final examination.

5. The facts of both the Writ Petitions Nos. 11905 of 2015 and 11582 of 2015 are more or less the same. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rules in both the Writ Petition Nos. 11905 of 2015 and 11582 of 2015 are as follows:

6. The petitioners appeared at the admission test for the BDS course as per the Medical and Dental Colleges Nitimala, 2011 having requisite combined Grade Point Average/GPA of minimum 8 in S.S.C. and H.S.C. examinations from the science faculty with at least 3.50 in any of the aforesaid examinations. The petitioners obtained above the cut-off' mark 105 out of 200. The petitioners got themselves admitted into the Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS) for the session 2013-2014 in their respective institutions and they have been participating regularly in their academic classes. Earlier Bangladesh Private Medical College Association (BPMCA), as the petitioner, filed Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 impugning the recommendations of a meeting dated 23.09.2013 held at the instance of respondent No. 1 increasing the minimum "cut-off' mark from 110 to 120 out of total marks of 200 for admission into the MBBS/BDS courses for the session 2013-2014. The respondent No. 1 earlier framed the Nitimala, 2011 for admission of students into the MBBS/BDS courses (hereinafter referred to as the Nitimala, 2011) stipulating the admission/qualification criteria for enrollment of students into the MBBS/BDS courses in all medical/dental colleges (public/private) in Bangladesh. Clause 2.2 of the Nitimala, 2011 states, inter alia, that an applicant must acquire a combined Grade Point Average (GPA) of minimum 8.00 in his/her respective SSC and HSC examinations from the Science Faculty provided that he/she does not carry less than CPA 3.50 in any of the aforesaid examinations. Again, respondent No. 1 by an office order dated 04.12,2012 stipulated admission criteria of the MBBS/BDS courses for the session 2012-2013 pursuant to which an applicant is required to have merit score of 110 for admission into the MBBS course and 105 into the BDS course. Respondent No. 2 issued an admission notification dated 31.8.2013 in the daily Prothom Alo dated 31.8.2013 for admission into the MBBS/BDS courses for the session 2013-2014. Clause No. 3 of the admission notification also stipulates that an applicant must have minimum GPA score 8.00 in both S.S.C. and H.S.C. examinations, but not less than 3.50 any of the examinations as per the Nitimala, 2011 as minimum criteria for eligibility for admission into the MBBS/BDS courses. The admission notification did not require any applicant for the sessions 2013-2014 to have minimum merit score of 120 at the time when admission notification was issued in the daily Prothom Alo dated 31.8.2013. In the meantime, respondent No. 1 by the notification dated 19.9.2013 informed that a meeting to be held on 23.9.2013 to determine the pass mark required to be achieved by the students of MBBS/BDS courses in the "admission test". In the meeting dated 23.9.2013 decision was taken to the effect that in order to be eligible for admission into the MBBS/BDS courses, an applicant must have a minimum "cut-off' mark 120 out of total marks of 200 for the session 2013-2014, thus introducing a new minimum qualification criteria for the "admission process" in the said courses for the session 2013-2014. Respondent No. 2 by his letter dated 07.1.2014 recommended that the minimum "merit score" for an applicant to be eligible for admission into the MBBS/BDS courses shall be fixed at "105". Thereafter respondent No. 1 by his order dated 02.02.2014 extended the deadline for admission into the MBBS/BDS until 15.2.2014. In Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014, a Division Bench of this Court made the Rule absolute and directed the respondents to allow the private medical colleges to admit the students willing to take admission into the MBBS course for the session 2013-2014 with a "cut-off' mark at 105.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 18.9.2014 passed in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014, the respondent No. 1 moved before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh and the Appellate Division after hearing the Civil Appeal No. 147 of 2015 along with Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1110 of 2015 and 1111 of 2015 upheld the judgment and order dated 18.9.2014 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 and dismissed the appeal and also held that 224 students who have already been admitted into 23 different private medical colleges are entitled to continue their study in the respective medical colleges where they got admission. All the petitioners have requisite educational qualification to get admission into the BDS course and they have been participating in their academic classes successfully and as such they are entitled to continue to their study of Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS) in their respective educational institutions. The respondents are required to be directed to give registration to the petitioners without further delay. Respondents are bound by the judgment and order of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 and also the judgment and order passed by the Appellate Division passed in Civil Appeal No. 147 of 2015.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the inaction of the respondents to give registration to the petitioners including other students of Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS) admitted into different Private Dental Colleges of Bangladesh securing above the cut-off mark 105 out of 200 have moved this Court and obtained the instant Rules Nisi.

9. Respondent No. 5 entered appearance in both the Writ Petitions by filing separate Affidavits-in-Oppositions controverting all the material statements made in the Writ Petition Nos. 11905 of 2015 and 11582. The common case of respondent No. 5, in short, in both the Writ Petition Nos. 11905 of 2015 and 11582 of 2015, is as follows:

10. The petitioners have no locus standi to file the instant writ petitions. The authority took a resolution that in order to get admission into the MBBSAIDS courses, the admission seekers must secure 120 marks out of 200 and the admission seekers must also secure 40 marks out of 100 in the written examination. If the minimum merit score is fixed at 105 out of 200 marks, an admission seeker getting 05 out of 100 marks in the written test shall have a possibility to get admission into the concern Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS) in the Private Dental Colleges of Bangladesh which is not desirable. The petitioners have totally failed to understand the content of the judgment and order passed by the Appellate Division. The judgment of the Appellate Division passed in Civil Appeal No. 147 of 2015 concerns only 224 students of different private medical colleges, who were the petitioners of the Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 and who were the admission seekers into the MBBS course. The petitioners being the admission seekers into the BDS course have no legal right to get the benefit of the said judgment. The grounds taken in the petition are not valid, lawful and tenable in the eye of law and as such both the Rules Nisi are liable to be discharged with costs.

Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners in both the writ petitions submits that all the petitioners have requisite educational qualifications to be eligible to get admission into the BDS course and that they have been participating in their academic classes successfully and as such they are entitled to continue their study of Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS) in their respective educational institutions. She further submits that in response to an advertisement floated by the respondent No. 2 in the daily Prothom Alo dated 31.82013, the petitioners having requisite qualifications applied for admission into the BDS course. She also submits that the petitioners obtained cut-off marks 105 as determined by respondent No. 2 in the meeting dated 04.12.2012 for admission into the MBBS/BDS courses for the session 2012-2013. She lastly submits that the petitioners having got the requisite qualifications are eligible to continue their study in BDS course and that the respondents are legally bound, to give registration to the petitioners.

12. Mr. A.F.M. Mesbahuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent No. 5 in both the writ petitions, on the other hand, submits that the present applications are not tenable in the eye of law. He further submits that the authority took a resolution that in order to get admission into the MBBS/BDS course, it was not enough for the admission seekers to get 120 cut off marks out of 200, rather the admission seekers must also get minimum 40 marks out of 100 in the written examination. He next submits that the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 and the judgment and order passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal No. 147 of 2015 with Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1110 of 2015 and 1111 of 2015 are directed for the admission seekers of MBBS course and that the petitioners being the admission seekers of BDS course are not entitled to get the benefit of the above judgments and orders of the High Court Division and the Appellate Division. The judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 (Annexure-H);

28. Against the decision dated 23.9.2013 (Annexure-B) taken by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the Bangladesh Private Medical College Association (BPMCA) filed a Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 challenging the raising of the minimum cut-off mark at 120 out of 200 for admission into the MBBS course for the session 2013-2014. It may be mentioned here that though the raising of cut-off mark at 120 was fixed for the admission of both the MBBS and the BDS courses, the BPMCA filed the Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 only for the students willing to take admission into the MBBS course. None from the students of BDS course challenged the raising of cut-off mark at 120. After hearing both the sides, a Division Bench of this Court held as under:

"The Nitimala in its flag end mentioned about a committee, which will be responsible implementing the Nitimala 2011, however, neither in the letter dated 04.12.2012, nor in any other letters of circular, we could find any mention about the committee, which clearly reflects that the respondents are acting Just at their own caprice and whim without bothering to adhere to their own Nitimala, and apart from that they are not even obliging their own letter dated 07,01.2014 for admission into MBBS and BM with the cut-off mark of 105. ……… as such, denying admission to students securing cut-off mark 105 and/or above is nothing but colourable exercise of power since it the respondents themselves have set the new cut-off mark for admission into MBBS and BDS for the academic session 2013-2014.

In the premises set forth above, we are of the view that the Rule deserves merit and the respondents be directed to allow the private medical colleges to admit students for the academic session 2013-2014 with a cut-off mark at 105."

29. The High Court Division by the above judgment in no uncertain terms held that the cut-off mark for the students for admission in the academic session 2013-2014 would be 105.

30. In our opinion the word, "students" mentioned in the judgment of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 would mean the "students" willing to take admission into the MBBS course. Because, the Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 was filed by the BPMCA challenging the raising of cut-off mark at 120 for the students willing to take admission into the MBBS course. But the decision taken in the meeting dated 23,9.2013 increasing the cut-off mark at 120 was directed for the students who were willing to take admission in both the MBBS and BDS courses.

31. So, with all fairness the direction of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 to allow the Private Medical Colleges to admit students for the academic session 2013-2014 with the cut-off mark at 105 would be applicable for the students willing to take admission into the MBBS course and it would not be applicable for the present petitioners as they are willing to take admission into the BDS course. However, even if we take that the cut-off mark 105 fixed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 is applicable only for the students willing to take admission into the MBBS course, the present petitioners will be equally benefited because they all have obtained mark above 105 in their admission test,

The judgment passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal No. 147 of 2015 with Civil Petition for Leave to Anneal Nos. 1110 of 2015 and 1111 of 2015 dated 16.9.2015 (Annexure-H1).

32. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division passed on 18.9.2014 in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014, a Civil Appeal No. 147 of 2015, Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1110 of 2015 and 1111 of 2015 were filed and the Appellate Division dismissed the appeal and held as under:

"Admittedly, the impugned decision raising the minimum "cut-off- mark from 110 to 120 was taken by a committee headed by the respondent No. 1 and not by the council, namely, Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council (BMDC) which has been formed as per law, namely, Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council Act, 2010. Section 5 of this Act shows that this Council (BMOC) is empowered to deal with almost all the matters relating to Medical and Dental Institutions including framing of guidelines etc. for admission to MB.B.S. and B.D.S. courses. The setting of "cut-off" mark for being eligible for admission to MB.B.S. and B.D.S. courses falls within theses powers of BMDC and as such the BMDC only is empowered to fix or set the minimum "cut-off" mark for being eligible for admission to these courses. Admittedly, the impugned decision raising the "cut-off" mark from 110 to 120 was not taken by this BMDC, rather if was taken by the respondent No. 1 and some other persons………….

So, it is apparent that the impugned decision raising the "cut-off" mark from 110 to 120 being not taken by the BMOC was coram non judice and as such illegal.

……………….

This civil appeal thus be dismissed with the above observations."

33. From the above decision of the Appellate Division, we find that the decision taken in the meeting dated 23.9.2013 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Annexure-B) was coram non-judice and illegal.

34. In the meeting dated 23,9.2013 (Annexure-B), the cut-off mark at 120 was fixed for MBBS/BDS courses. But this decision dated 23.9.2013 has been declared illegal and coram non judice by the Appellate Division. So, legally there is no existence of the decision of the meeting dated 23.9.2013 and as such there is no existence of the cut-off mark 120 anymore.

35. In the Nitimala, 2011 (Annexure-C) there is no mention of cut-off mark at all. In the decision dated 04.12.2012 taken by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Annexure-D), the cut-off mark was fixed at 110 for the students willing to take admission into the MBBS course and at 105 for the students willing to take admission into the BDS course. But this cut-off mark was fixed for the students who were willing to take admission for the session 2012-2013. This cut-off mark 110 and 105 for the students willing to take admission into the MBBS/BDS courses shall not be applicable for the petitioners as they are willing to take admission for the session 2013-2014.

<u>36. In fact, after the judgment passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal No. 147 of 2015, there was no in existence of any cut-off mark for the students willing to take admission into MBBS/BDS courses for the sessions 2013-2014. Because the cut-off mark 120 fixed by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in its meeting dated 23.9.2013 for the session 2013-2014 has been declared illegal and coram non-judice by the Appellate Division by its judgment and order dated 16.9.2015. Precisely, the cut-off mark 105 fixed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 is applicable for the students willing to take admission into the MBBS course and this cut-off mark 105 fixed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 is not applicable for the students willing to take admission into the BDS course, because Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 was filed by the BPMCA for the students willing to take admission into the MBBS course only.</u>

<u>37. However, through vigorous search, we find one letter dated 7.1,2014 (Annexure-G) issued by the Director of the Directorate of Health, This letter dated 7.1.2014, was addressed to the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare by the Director of the Directorate of Health. In this letter, the Director of the Directorate of Health recommended to fix up the cut-off mark at 105 for the students willing to take admission into both the MBBS and the BDS courses and also recommended to extend the period of admission upto 31.1.2014. In response to the letter dated 7.1.2014, issued by the Director of the Directorate of Health, the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare did not say a word about the fixation of cut-off mark at 105 but extended the time for admission upto 15.7.2014.</u>

38. For proper appreciation, the letter dated 7.1.2014 issued by the Director of the Directorate of Health, addressed to the Secretary Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is quoted below which runs as under:

২। ডীন, মেডিসিন ফ্যাকাল্টি, ঢাকা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়, ঢাকা।

৩। রেজিষ্ট্রার, ঢাকা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়, ঢাকা।

<u>40. From the above, it is clear that the recommendations of the Director of Health to fix up the curt-off mark at 105 was not accepted by the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. However, the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare extended the period of admission upto 15.2.2014.</u>

41. So, taking everything into consideration, we do not find any cut-off mark for the students willing to take admission into the BDS courses for the session 2013-2014.

<u>42. Since there is no cut-off mark for the students willing to take admission into the BDS course for the session 2013-2014, we may go back to the Nitimala, 2011 (Annexure-C) and the advertisement dated 31.8.2013 (Annexure-E). In the Nitimala, 2011 (Annexure-C) the condition laid down for admission into the MBBS/BDS courses is that the students must obtain GPA 8.00 both in HSC and SSC examinations but not less than GPA 3.50 in any of the examinations. In the advertisement for admissions into the MBBS/BDS courses (Annexure-E) for the session 2013-2014, it has also been stated that the students willing to get admission into the MBBS/BDS courses must get GPA 8.00 in both HSC and SSC examinations but not less than GPA 3.50 in any of the examinations. The petitioners in both the Writ Petitions have got CPA 8.00 and they have got not less than GPA 3.50 in any of the HSC/SSC examinations. So, they are eligible to get admission into the BDS course. They have already got admission into the BDS course in different medical colleges / dental unit and they have been continuing their study till date. The petitioners are the admission seekers for the BDS course. Although there is no compulsion for the petitioners to get the cut-off mark 105 for admission into the BDS course for the session 2013-2014, we just want to record that all the petitioners got minimum 105 marks in their admissions test.</u>

43. The petitioners have been successfully studying in the BDS course in various medical colleges. Therefore, there is no earthly reason to refuse the registration number of the petitioners.

44. Considering all these facts and circumstances and the discussions made hereinbefore, we find merit in both the Rules.

45. Accordingly, both the Rules issued in Writ Petition Nos. 11905 of 2015 and 11582 of 2015 are made absolute.

46. The respondents are directed to give registration number to the petitioners immediately.

47. There is no order as to costs.

End.
