full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J.:- This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 24.10.2001 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1586 of 1996 making the rule absolute setting aside the judgment and decree dated 16.1.1996 in Title Appeal No. 245 of 1993 of the Additional District Judge, Comilla reversing the final decree dated 5.7.1993 drawn up by the Senior Assistant Judge, Comilla Sadar in Partition Suit No. 268 of 1958.

2. The predecessor of the respondents filed a suit for partition being Partition Suit No. 288 of 1958 for partition of a share of 4 annas 17 gondas 1-2/3 Krants in the disputed land stating inter alia, that the disputed land belonged to the 3 brothers namely, Naimuddin, Ali Mohammad and Mohammad Ali in equal shares. As Mohammad Ali was minor and lived jointly with his eldest brother Naimuddin, two third was recorded in the name of Naimuddin who died leaving behind two sons and two daughters (defendant No. 10 and predecessor of defendant Nos. 11-16) Ali Mohammad as well sold 10 gondas to Naimuddin and 10 gondas to Asrab Ali; that Asrab Ali sold 10 gondas to defendants 18 and 10 gondas to Mohammad Ali; that Mohammad Ali gifted his 10 gondas to plaintiff No. 9 and Asrab Ali's heirs also sold their shares. The aforesaid 3 brothers together sold 2 kanis, 5 gondas to Akub Ali, the father of defendant No. 17 on 15 Sravan, 1370 B.S. Mohammad Ali died unmarried and he gifted his entire share to plaintiff No. 9 on 16th Magh, 1333 B.S and delivered possession. The respondents claiming their share in the property demanded partition from the defendants. That the defendants 1-8 are heirs of Ali Mohammad and second party defendants are purchasers from him. Hence plaintiff s share is 4 annas 17 gondas 1-2/3 krants. He demanded partition from the defendants but they did not comply. Hence the suit.

3. Defendant Nos. 1-5 and 23-25 contested the suit filing written statement stating that they only claim saham for their alleged share in the suit property.

4. The suit was, however, contested by the defendant No. 17 who was the predecessor of the appellants contending, inter alia, that Naimuddin, Ali Mohammad and Mohammad Ali sold 2 Kanies, 5 gondas of Plot Nos. 208, 209, 214 and 215 to Akub Ali on 15th Servant 1307 B.S and Ali Mohammad sold 15 gondas of Plot Nos. 208 and 209 to him on 22nd Magh, 1313 B.S and that Akub Ali gifted all these lands along with other lands to defendant No. 17 in 1353 B.S and delivered possession to him and he possessed, the same denying the plaintiffs claim and the predecessor of the petitioners claim a saham for 2 kandies 12½ gondas in case the partition is allowed.

5. The said suit was decreed in preliminary form on 30.12.1969 against which Abdul Gani, defendant No. 17 preferred Title Appeal No. 49 of 1960 before the learned District Judge, Comilla which was subsequently transferred to the Subordinate Judge for disposal, who allowed the appeal by modifying the judgment and decree of the trial Court to the extent that the plot No. 209/3, 214, 215 be left out of partition by his judgment and decree dated 30.7.1960. Against the aforesaid judgment of the appellate Court, the respondents preferred Second Appeal No. 201 of 1961 before the High Court Division and subsequently the Second Appeal was dismissed for non-prosecution on 2.2.1978. Thereafter the respondent prayed for making the said preliminary decree final by appointing Advocate Commissioner. Accordingly Mr. Kabirudding Ahmed was appointed Advocate Commissioner but he failed to file his report for a long time and the parties prayed for cancellation of his appointment and accordingly his appointment was cancelled on 8.4.1993. Thereafter, Mr. Abdul Matin Mazumder was appointed as Advocate Commissioner who submitted his report on 5.6.1993. The learned Assistant Judge thereafter made the said preliminary decree final on 5.7.1993 in Partition Suit No. 288 of 1958 making the report, saham, chita and field book as part of the final decree.

6. That against the aforesaid final decree, the appellants herein preferred Title appeal No. 245 of 1993 before the learned District Judge, Comilla on the ground, inter alia, that the aforesaid decree has been vitiated in allotting the share to the respondents herein plot No. 209/3, 214 and 215 which ere excluded by the learned Appellate court in the previously filed Title Appeal No. 49 of 1960.

7. The learned District Judge thereafter transferred the said Title Appeal No. 245 of 1993 to the Court of the Additional District Judge who upon hearing the parties allowed the appeal by setting aside the final decree dated 5.7.1993 by his judgment and decree dated 6.1.1996

8. That the respondents being aggrieved moved the High Court Division and the rule issued in Civil revision No. 1586 of 1996 was made absolute and hence this appeal by leave.

Leave was granted by this Court to consider:

Mr. Faruque Ahmed, the learned Counsel appearing for the leave petitioners, argued that the learned Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the plot No. 299/3, 214 and 215 are not included in the saham of any party, overlooking the fact that the Advocate Commissioner filed report of investigation including the aforesaid 3 plots in residuary saham in violation of the direction of the lower appellate Court in Title Appeal No. 49 of 1960 for exclusion of these plots from the present suit.

9. Mr. Faruque Ahmed, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in not considering the saham, Chitta book of the Advocate Commissioner as well as report wherein the plot Nos. 209/3, 214 and 215 have been included as the divisible land violating the order of the appellate Court and the learned Advocate Commissioner has allotted the saham on the basis of faulty division which is much less than actual divisible land inasmuch as total 8.59 acres of land for division is palpably, erroneous and incorrect the separate saham must very less if the above 3 plots are deducted from the divisible land and hence the whole measurement of the Advocate Commissioner is faulty.

<u>10. Mr. Harendra Nath Nandi, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 1-4 submitted that the High Court Division committed no error in placing the plot Nos. 209/3, 214 and 215 in the residuary saham list as because the appellate Court passed decree modifying the trial Court's decree to the extent that the plot Nos. 209/3, 214 and 215 are left out of partition and that these plots were not expunged from the schedule of the plaint.</u>

11. Admittedly, the suit land originally belonged to Naimuddin, Ali Mohammad and Mohammaed Ali, each having 1/3 re share. Mohammad Ali was under the guardian of Naimuddin and Accordingly 2/3rd share of the suit was recorded in the name of Naimuddin, Plaintiff and his brother respondent No. 9 are the sons of Naimuddin and defendant No. 10 is the daughter and defendant Nos. 11-16 are successors in interest of another deceased daughter. Ali Mohammad Sold 10 gonda to Naimuddin out of his 1/3 rd share. Plaintiffs accordingly claimed their shares in the suit land of the land of Naimuddin. The trial Court, accordingly, decreed the suit in preliminary form on contest against defendant No. 17 on contest against defendant Nos. 1-5 and 23-25 and in presence of and without contest against defendant Nos. 9-11, 18-26, 32 and 41-45 and exparte against the rest. The trial Court accordingly decreed the suit as under:

“Plaintiff and defendant No. 9, shall get a saham each for a share of 4 annas 8 gondas 3 karas 2/3 krant minus 8 gs. 3 karas 12/3 kraits of lands, defendant 10 shall get a saham for a share of 17 gs. 3 karas 1/3 krant minus 5 gs. 21/3 krants of lands and defendant 11-16 shall get a like saham, defendant No. 18 shall get a saham for 21 cents and defendant 26-30 a saham for 68 cents and defendant No. 32 shall get a saham for 9 cents, parties shall amicable partition lands of their respective shares within one month from date. In default a commissioner shall issue to effect the partition by mets and bounds on either party's depositing necessary money for it, having regard to the convenience and present possession of the parties. Parties shall bar costs of the preliminary and final decrees in proportion to their respective shares.

12. On appeal the judgment and decree of the trial Court was modified to the extent that plot No. 209/3, 214 and 215 are left out of partition and in respect of plot No. 208/3 the defendant No. 17 do get saham to the extent of .48 decimals thereof from the list more or less on the land shown by the commissioner in his map so far as it perceivable and the defendant Nos. 26-30 did not get any saham, their claim 2/3rd share of this said 46 decimals of plot No. 208/3 being left open the portion of the share of the plaintiff and of their defendant was found by the learned Munsif is left undistributed. Thereafter the learned Advocate Commissioner drawn up the final decree affecting the partition of the suit land as under:

“ডিক্রীকৃত ভূমির মধ্যে প্রাথমিক ডিক্রী মার্মানুযায়ী বাদী মোঃ ২৫-১⁄২ শতক ভূমি পত্তনীয় বটে। বাদীর উক্ত ভূমির জন্য এবং আমার কৃত নকসার ও চিঠার ৮-৯-১৬১৭ (ক),১/৩৮/৩৬/১৪/২২/২৩/২৮/২৭(ক)২৫/৫৩/৫৪/৫৫/৫৬/৬০/৩০/৩১/৩২/৩৩/৩৪/ নচ ঠিকার ভূমি এবং এজমালী ভূমি সহ মোঃ ২.৫২-১⁄২ শতক ভূমি বাদীর ও ১০ নং বিবাদীর ছাহামে দেওয়া গেল। ডিক্রীকৃত ভূমির মধ্যে প্রাথমিক ডিক্রীর মর্মানুযায়ী ৯/১১ নং বিবাদীগণ মোঃ ২.৪৬-১⁄২ শতক ভূমি পত্তনীয় বটে। বিবাদীগনের উক্ত ভূমির জন্য আমার কৃত নকসার ও চিঠার ১/৫/৬/৮/(ক)৭/১৮/১৪(ক)/৩৮(ক)/৩৪(খ)/৩০(ক) /৪০/২৪/২১/২৬/২৭/৫১/৫২/৫৭/ ৫৮/৫৯/৩৫(ক)/৩৬(ক)/৩৭/৩৮(ক)/৪৪ নং চিঠিার ভূমি এবং এজমালি ভূমিসহ মোঃ ২.৪৬-১⁄২ শতক ভূমি বিবাদীগণের ছাহামে দেওয়া গেল। ডিক্রীকৃত ভূমি মধ্যে অবশিষ্ট অংশীদার বিবাদীগনের মধ্যে এজমালিতে দখল তছরুপের জন্য আমার কৃত ছাহাম বহির ৩ নং ছাহামের ভূমি এবং আমার কৃত নকসার ও চিঠার ৩/৪/১৫ নং ভূমি মোঃ ৪১ শতক এজমালিতে রাখা হইল।

ডিক্রীকৃত ভুমির মধ্যে অবশিষ্ট অংশীদার বিবাদীগণের জন্য মোঃ ৩.৬০ শকত ভূমি অবশিষ্ট ছাহামে রাখা হইল। উক্ত ভূমি আমার কৃত ছাহাম বহির ৪নং অবশিষ্ট ছাহামে এবং আমার কৃত নকসার ও চিঠার ১০/১১/১২/১৩/১৭/১৯/২০/২৯/৩৯/৪২/৪৫/৪৭/ ৪৮/৪৯/৫০ /৬১/৬৩ নং চিঠার ভূমি মোঃ ৩.৬০ শতক রহিল।

বন্টনকার্য সময় আমি পক্ষগণের দখল পূর্ব দখল দখলের সুবিধা অসুবিধা, রকমের তারতম্য ও মূল্যের তারতম্য যথাসম্ভব বিবেচনা করিয়া বন্টন কা্র্য্য করিয়াছি।”

From the above, it appears, inter alia, that pursuant to the preliminary decree the plaintiff and his wife have been given a saham of 2.52½ decimals of land and The defendant Nos. 9-11 were given their share of 2.46½. An area of.41 decimals of land as specified in the sketch map has been left over in ejmali for use and enjoyment of plaintiff and defendants. Rest 3.60 decimals of the suit land has been kept in residuary saham of the other co sharer defendant and the distribution of the sahams of the co sharers are more fully detailed in the report and sketch map of the Civil Court Commissioner forming part of the final decree in the suit.

In view of the above, we do not find any substance in the submission of the learned Counsel for the appellant for our interference with the impugned judgment.

The appeal is accordingly, dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule issued calling upon the plaintiff-respondent-opposite party Nos.1-11 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 30.06.2005 and 07.07.2005 respectively passed by the learned Additional District judge, Gazipur in Civil Appeal No. 81 of 1997 affirming those dated 16.04.1997 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur in Civil suit No. 112 of 1994 should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this quit may seem fit and proper. 
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the predecessor of the present opposite party Nos.1-11 as plaintiffs initially instituted Title Suit being No. 420 of 1978 in the 1st Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for getting partition of the suit land in respect of a separate Saham of 6.3 ½ acres of land. That suit was contested by the present petitioners who are the defendant Nos. 7-16 of the suit. In that suit the defendant Nos.19-20 also contested by filing separate written statement. That suit subsequently was transferred to the 1st Court of subordinate Judge, Gazipur and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 967 of 1985 and after trial the suit was decreed on 28.02.1990 in part allocating a Saham of 4.02½  acres of land in favour of the plaintiffs. Being aggrieved the plaintiff-opposite parties preferred Title Appeal No. 72 of 1990 in the court of learned District Judge, Gazipur while the defendant-petitioners did not prefer any cross- objection against the judgment and decree. The appeal was transferred to the 1st Court of learned Additional District Judge, Gazipur and after hearing, having found that the issues not being properly adjudicated allowed the appeal and sent back the suit on remand to the trial court. The learned Subordinate Judge 1st Court, Gazipur after getting the suit on remand renumbered the suit as Title Suit No. 112 of 1994 and after hearing passed the judgment and decree dated 16.04.1997 allocating the Saham of 6.03½  acres of land in favour of the plaintiff-opposite parties with further allocation of a Saham of .41 acres of land in favor of the defendant No.19-20. The case of opposite-parties as plaintiffs of Civil Suit No. 112 of 1994 is such that the disputed property originally belonged to one Osman, Abdul, Abbas and Sadhu in equal shares who are four full brothers. The C.S. Khatian stands recorded in their names in four anas share each but the name of four brother's father Sk. Mohor has been wrongly written in the remark column. The further case of the plaintiff-opposite-parties is such that Sheik Mohar Ali was not alive at the time of C.S. operation. The C.S. Khatian Nos.06 and 46 though was recorded in the name of Sheikh Mahar Ali but in fact that would have been recorded in the name of two sons of sheikh Mohar, Alefuddin and Ainuddin. Subsequently after the death of Osman his two sons and the defendant No.6 and one daughter Moyoarjan along with mother Motijan Bibi inherited the property. One son Abdul Hamid died leaving behind six sons the defendants No. 1-5 and one Mazharul Haque. Mazharul Haque transferred his share in favour of the plaintiff No.1 and the plaintiff No.1 exhausted that land after transferring the same in favour of the defendants. Abbas died leaving two brothers but during his life time he transferred his entire share in favour of his brother Sadhu by a transfer deed dated 13.10.1943. Subsequently Abdul left this country for Assam of India and used to reside therein with his family. The share of Abdul in C.S. Khatian No. 43 has been auction sold in favour one Amullaa Ghosh. Abdur Rahim purchased the land form Amulla and the successor of Abdul Hamid, Sirajul transferred his share in favour of his five brothers and Nurul Haque transferred his share in favour his four brothers Sadhu died leaving one son the plaintiff No. 1 and two daughters Moziran and Kulshum. The two daughters of Sadhu transferred their share in favour of the plaintiff No.1. During the life time of Sadhu his one daughter Sabjan died and as such the heirs of sabjan does not inherit the property of sheikh Sadhu. The wife of Sheikh Sadhu made a Heba-Bil-Ewaj deed in respect of 2 arias share in favour of Mofizuddin on 20.11.1960. Kulshum Bibi transferred her share in favour of the plaintiff Nos. 2-5 and the daughter of Abdul Humid Kadiron Nesa transferred her share in favour of the defendants. The property left behind Sheikh Sadhu was inherited by the plaintiffs who acquiring the suit land by way of inheritance and purchase possess the same in ejmaili with the defendants. The plaintiffs by way of several purchase deeds acquired the land in the disputed holding and the land measuring 5.85 acres had been owning and possessing by the plaintiffs. Furthermore; in respect of the land described in schedule "Kha" the original owners were Sheikh Osman and Sheikh Sadhu in 8 anas share each. The plaintiffs possessing their land with the heirs of Sheikh Osman. In respect of 24 decimals of land in plot No.99 and 0.27 decimals of land in plot No. 86 of the C.S. Khatian Na. 43 one surendra Nath purchased before C.S. operation and that land has been excluded from the schedule of the plaint. During S.A. and R.S. operation the land has been recorded in ejmali with the names of the defendants. The plaintiffs due to their difficulty in ejmali possession requested the defendants to make amicable partition but being failure instituted the suit. 
3. The contrary case of the contesting defendants No. 7-16 in brief is such that the disputed, property belonged to Sheikh Mohar Ali and after the death of Mohar Ali his four sons Osman and three others along with three daughters Nur Banu, Rahima and Ahatannesa became the heirs of Sheikh Mohar Ali. Abbas Ali transferred his 1.23 acres of land in favour of one Darbesh Ali and Ahatan Nese by a Heba-Bil-Ewaz. Abdul and Rahima transferred 0.94 acres of land in favour of Darbesh Ali, Ahatan Nesa and Montaj on 24.12.1943. Osman Ali died leaving his two sons Abdul Hamid and Kashimuddin and one daughter Mayor Jan. Sheikh Sadhu transferred 61½ decimals of land on 13.12.1943. At the death of Abdul Hamid his six sons the defendant Nos. 1-5 along with one Mazaharul Haque and two daughters became his heirs. The plaintiff No.1 transferred 47 decimals of land in favour of the defendant Nos.1, 2, 4 and 5. The share of Abdul was auction purchased by one Amulla Chandra in a Rent Suit being No.1772 of 1935 which was subsequently transferred by Amulla in favour of Abdul Hamid by a Kabala deed dated 16.12.1937. The defendant No. 2 purchased 17 ½  decimals of land by a kabla deed dated 24.06.1976 from Kaherun Nesa. One Abdur Sabur purchased .52 ½ acres of land from the son of Abdul Humid on 30.12.1974. Abdur Sabur subsequently transferred his land in favour of the defendant Nos. 2, 4 and 5 and the defendant No. 2 by a kabla deed dated 30.12.1974 purchased 14 decimals of land from Nurul Huq and others. Afazuddin Munshi father of these defendants purchased 0.69 acres of land form one Kunja Bahari Pal by a purchase deed dated 13.02.1947 which was acquired by Kunja Bahari Pal from Abdur Sabur and Abdul Humid. The defendant Nos.7-9 acquired 10 4/3 decimals of land by purchase on 2.7.1977 and the defendant No. 1 sold 29 decimals of land in favour of Mazaharul Haque and the defendant Nos. 2-5. The defendant No.3 transferred 17 ½ decimals of and in favour of defendant No.1, 2, 4 & 5 along with Mazharul by a Kabla deed dated 4.12.1963. The defendant Nos.7-9 purchased 44 decimals of land from the defendant No. 2 on 28.06.1978 and 35 decimals of land on 27.05.1978. The defendant’s No. 7-9 also purchased 35 decimals of land form the defendant No.4 and after acquiring those lands possessed the same in ejmali with other co-shares. The further case of the defendant Nos.7-9 in short is such that the son of Sheikh Mohar Ali, Osman died leaving behind Abdul Hamid and others. Abdul Hamid died leaving his heirs Kadirun Nesa and others and Kadirun Nesa transferred 17 ½ decimals of land in favour of Shamsul Haque on 24.06.1976. The brother of Shamsul Haque, Serajul transferred his share in favour of Nurul Haque and others by a sale deed dated 04.12.1963. Subsequently; by a deed of exchange dated, 20.12.1980 Abdul Ali handed over possession of that land in favour of defendant Mostafa and others. Kosimuddin transferred 26 decimals of land in favour of Abdur Razzaque. The daughter of Sheikh Mohar, Ahatan Nesa died leaving her son Darog Ali and Darog Ali by a kabla deed dated 24.12.1981 transferred 8 ½ decimals of land in favour of defendant Mostafa and others. Sheikh Sadhu One of the son of Sheikh Mahar transferred 61 decimals of land in favour of Abdul Hamid by a sale deed dated 13.02.1943 and 14 decimals of land in favour of Md. Abdul Ali by a sale deed dated 13.12.1943 and after the death of Sukur Mahmud, the defendant Nos.17-18 became the parties to the suit who has created a forged deed to deprive other heirs. The S.A. record has been wrongly prepared to that effect. The defendant No. 18 possess 31 decimals of land in suit plot No.109. That the defendant Nos.19-25 prayed for a separate Saham in respect of 19 decimals of land. The defendant No. 20 prayed for 95 2/3 decimals of land in the disputed holding. 
4. The trial court holding trial decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 16.04.1997. Being aggrieved the defendant Nos.7-16 preferred title appeal No.81 of 1997 in the court of learned District Judge, Gazipur which was transmitted to the first court of learned Additional District Judge, Gazipur and the learned appellant court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30.06.2005 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 
5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the defendant-appellant-petitioners has preferred this revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedures and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay and status-quo. 
6. Mr. Md. Mozammel Hoque, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of petitioners while Mr. Md. Shamsul Alam the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties. 
7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned Courts below committed error of law in deciding the fate of the Suit and its subsequent appeal in favour of the plaintiffs which is not legal, just and proper. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Appellate court failed to assess the evidence on records and appreciate the actual position of lass in its true perspective and that there has been non-consideration of material facts as well as misreading and non-reading of evidence resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the trial court committed error of law in holding that the suit land belonged to Osman Ali and his three brothers which is against with the pleadings of the parties and evidence on records and both the courts below wrongly held that the defendants admitted the ownership of Osman of his brothers in the suit land rather the defendant Nos.7-16, 19-20 and 25 clearly asserted in their written statements that the suit land originally belonged to Sheikh Mohar Ali, father of Osman and his brothers. The same is also appears in the plaint of a plaintiffs and it has been stated by them that the name of Sheikh Mohar Ali has been wrongly recorded in the remark column of the khatian. The learned Advocate further submits that all the P.Ws. during their deposition admitted the possession of the defendants in the disputed property which is not considered by the courts below and the concerned C.S. Khatian marked exhibit -1 shows that the suit land belonged to Sheikh Mohar Ali. In respect of getting separate Saham in the suit holding the question of possession in allocating Saham in favour of the defendant-petitioners has been ignored by the courts below and in this context the learned Advocate referred a decision of our Apex Court reported in 17 DLR (AD) 57 wherein it is held that under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure the High Court Division is empowered to interfere with the concurrent observation & findings of the courts below when it is noticed that there has been error of law or misreading & non-reading of material evidence resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Moreover; the evidence which were adduced from the sides of the respective parties not properly evaluated by the learned court in allocation of separate Sahain and without cancellation of kabala dated 3.11.1943 marked Exhibit- "চ" the plaintiffs are not in position to have any relief as prayed for. It is further submitted from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the claim of the plaintiffs is absolutely false, fabricated and motivated in view of their own admission made in their title deed marked Exhibit-4, where in they have asserted that they obtained the suit land by way of inheritance. P.W.1 admits that the name of Sheikh Mohor has been inserted in the C.S. khotian and thereby it is clear that the claim of the plaintiffs is barred by the principle of estoppel and it can be legitimately held that the suit land belonged to Sheikh Mohar Ali, who died leaving four sons and three daughters which is admitted by P.W. 1 in his cross examination. These sons and daughters of Sheikh Mohar Ali inherited the suit land in the following manner in schedule

8. The learned Advocate Mr. Haque also submits that it is found that the plaintiff’s predecessor Sadhu did not acquire any title over the land of Exhibit-4. Sheikh Sadhu, son of Sk. Mohar inherited 1.1344 acres of land in schedule 'A'. Out of this area Sadhu sold to A. Hamid-son of Osman 0.61 acres of land vide Exhibit-জ (Za). Subsequently; Sadhu also sold (vide exhibit-য) 0.14 acres of land to one Abdul Ali. Sadhu again sold jointly 0.23 acres of land to one Afazuddin vide kobala deed marked as Exhibit-স (Sa)-১.

10. The learned Counsel lastly submits that the defendant Nos.7-16 claimed 2.2288 acres of land both by inheritance and purchase and Afzuddin died intestate leaving defendant Nos.7-16 as heirs but the learned courts below wrongly held that the defendants did not acquire title by the exhibits ‘চ’ ‘ভ’ ‘ট’ and ‘র’। 
11. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite patties submits that in the disputed holding the area of total land is 9.11 acres and out of that the plaintiff-opposite-parties prayed for a separate Saham comprising an area of 6.03 ¼ acres of land. He further submits on behalf of the opposite-parties that both the trial court as well as the appellate court in their findings and decisions evaluated all the evidence on records correctly in its total approach and perspective. In sifting the evidence both oral and documentary and the assessment of evidence which is done is proper and lawful in the eye of law. There is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which it can be held that the plaintiffs are not entitled to get the relief in allocating their separate Salim as prayed for. It is the concurrent findings of the courts below that the deed dated 03.11.1943 marked exhibit- "Cha" from the side of the defendants is not a genuine document. It is antedated and beyond the pleadings 'of the defendants. The C.S. khatian 43 which is Exhibit -1 is not challenged form the side of the defendants and it stands recorded in the names of four brothers in 4 (four) anas share each. This khatian has a presumptive value of correctness and if it is not correct the other heirs of Sheikh Mohar would have been raised objection against it. In this context; the learned Advocate referred a decision of a Division Bench reported in 61 DLR 18. It appears from the connected documents that Exhibit-4 was executed on 27.09.1943 and its registration has been completed under Section 60 of the Registration Act on 13.12.1943 A.D. thence, Exhibit 4 was executed earlier with that of Exhibit "Cha" and both the two documents appears to have been executed by the same vendor. Under Section 47 of the Registration Act Exhibit-4 is a valid document which was duly effected on the date of its execution. Furthermore; it is concurrent findings of both the courts below that Mozammel and Mozaharul Haque is the some individual having two names. 
12. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the case records, exhibited documents, deposition of the witnesses and all other connected papers. 
13. On perusal of the case records I have come-across from the evidence that the witness No.6 for the plaintiffs is that Mozammel Haque alias Mozarul Haque who has deposed before the trial court and states in support of the plaintiffs pleadings. As regard the testimony of the plaintiff Abul Hossain which was agitated from the side of the defendants it transpires that the plaintiff No.1 Abul Hossain in his examination-in-chief admitted that the defendant Nos.7-9 have purchased excess land than that of the actual quantum of land. This contention despite has been denied from the side of the defendants but having gone through the entire testimony of the plaintiff Abul Hossain I find that the plaintiff Abut Hossain specifically said, “বিবাদী পক্ষ ৭, ৮ ও ৯ অধিক জমি ক্রয় করিয়াছেন।” Moreover, with regard to Exhibit-"ছ" it appears that Sheikh Sadhu, son of Sheikh Mohar Ali is the only person who inherited the entire land of Patijan Bibi inasmuch as at the time of death of Patijan, Sheikh Sadhu was the only surviving heir. 
14. Securitizing the case records it further appears that there has been a concurrent findings & decision of both the court's below that the plaintiffs are entitled to get a separate Saham in respect of 6.03 ½ acres of land in consultation of both the two documentary evidence marked Exhibit -"4" and Exhibit-"চ" respectively. The trial court as well as the appellate court relied upon Exhibit-4 of the plaintiffs. It further transpires from the case records that the trial court considering Exhibit-7 observed, Kasimuddin although sold out 132 acres of land to Mofizuddin by a transfer deed dated 12.12.1980 ever then the plaintiffs would get .65 acres of land by virtue of that deed marked as Exhibit-7 since the vendor had transferable share only with that extent of land. The trial court also observed that by Exltibit-6/1 Mozirun Nesa transferred 06 decimals of land by kabla deed dated 07.11.1975 in fav6r of the plaintiffs and by Ext-6/2, Abdul Haque sold out 28 ½ decimals of land by kabla deed No.7596 dated 11.09.1979 to the plaintifs, by Ext.6/3, Abdul Haque also sold out 28 ½ decimals of land by a sale deed bearing No.7601 dated 13.09.1978 to the plaintiffs and by Ext-8, Ahatan Nesa transferred 40 decimals of land by a sale deed bearing No. 19327 dated 20.11.1960 to the plaintiffs and by Ext.9, Misiron Nesa sold out 64 ½ decimals of land by another sale deed bearing No.6748 dated 15.06.1970 to Mafiz Uddin, Abul Hossain, Mosharaf Hossain and Abdul Goni and by Ext.9/1, Kulsum Nesa sold out 64½ decimals of land by a deed bearing No.10421 to Basiran Nesa (mother of the plaintiff opposite parties), Abul Hossain, Mosharaf Hossain and Abdul Goni and lastly; by Ext.11, the plaintiff-opposite parties purchased 17½ decimals of land from Serajul Haque. Hence; the trial Court calculated the share of the plaintiff -opposite parties as follows:
