full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J: This Rule, at the instance of the defendants, arises out of the judgment and order dated 6.4.86 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Madaripur in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 139 of 1984 reversing those dated 12.9.84 of the Munsif, 1st Court, Madaripur in Title Suit No. 170 of 1983.

2. The plaintiff filed the suit for declaration that the ex-parte decree dated 1.3.77 passed in Title Suit No. 70 of 1974 and the judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 145 of 1951 and the sole-decree, in Rent Suit No. 22 of 1957 are null and void, in operation, without any basis, collusive and not binding on the plaintiff and for a further declaration that the suit land is an enemy property stating, inter alia, that the suit land measuring 1.18 decimals of land of Khatian No. 22, Mouza Sukani in which Sailabala had /8/ annas raiyati interest, Anupanm and Manupama Debi had -/8/- annas interest. The said recorded owners were in possession of the suit land in whose names the kahtian was finally prepared and published. The entire interest of Sailabala was transferred to the plaintiff by registered Kabala dated 29.2.1957 and handed over possession thereof wherein the plaintiff has been residing by constructing houses, planting trees. Anupama and Manupama Debi prior to their leaving this country handed over possession of their annas interest to the plaintiff and subsequently the same became enemy property. The plaintiff being co-sharer appalled for the same which was leased out to him on local enquiiy in Lease. 'Case Nos. 37 and 38 of 1967-68. The plaintiff on payment of the lease money became rightful possessor thereof and has been possessing the same by planting trees and rearing fish in the pond. .59 decimals out of 1.18 decimals were acquired by the Public Health Department and the rest .39 decimals is left with the plaintiff on the basis of said purchase and lease. The defendant no. 1 on certain false averments filed Title Suit No.70 of 1974 and obtained an ex pane decree taking the advantage of the absence of the plaintiff which was subsequently set aside on contest restoring the suit to its original file and number but upon a revision before the learned District Judge at the instance of the defendant no. 1, the revision was allowed maintaining the ex-parte decree. On a further .revision by the Government in this Court, the said order was maintained and as such the plaintiff could not take any step earlier for setting aside the ex-parte decree and the limitation can be over came by filing application under section 5 of the Limitation Act. Had the plaintiff been able to produce the evidence, the defendant No. 1 would not have been able to obtain the decree and as such prayed for declaring the said ex-parte decree dated 1.3.77 as null, void, in operative etc. Plaintiffs further case is that one Kartile Chandra Chattapaddya filed Rent Suit No. 22 of 1957 against the defendant No. 1 and obtained a sole-decree on the assertion that Anupama- and Manupama leased cut their land in favour of him and prayed for setting aside the said sole-decree which has not affected the interest of the plaintiff. The plaintiff further alleged that the defendant no. 1 has also disclosed about a decree in favour of defendant no. 1 in Title Suit No: 145 of 1951. There was no service of notice upon the defendants .of that suit and the decree was obtained by fraudulent suppression of summons/notice and has prayed for declaring the said decree as void, in operative etc/The plaintiff further alleged that since 1967 the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land by paying rent to the enemy property authority. The plaintiff further alleged that in the event of an auction dated 30.5.67 in Rent Execution Case No. -167 of 1956 the suit land was auction purchased by one Mominuddin Mollah and the plaintiff filed sale set aside Case No. 78. of 1957 under the provision of section 174 of the Bengal Tenancy 'Act and the same was. accordingly set aside and the plaintiff paid the rent due and has been possessing the suit land on payment of rent. As the suit land has been declared as enemy property the plaintiff obtained the pattan. The Amalnama of the defendant no. 1 is forged and antedated .and the plaintiff having been threatened with dispossession in the first part of Baisak, 1390 B.S. the plaintiff was :obliged to file the suit.

3. The defendant nos. 1 and 2 'appeared in the suit, and filed an application under Order 7, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure denying the allegations made in the plaint stating, inter alia, that one Jahura-Bibi, vendor of the defendant not 2 and 3, filed Title Suit No. 70 of 1974 for declaration that the settlement in favour of the plaintiff is illegal, void, fraudulent and without jurisdiction and obtained the decree on 1.3.77 and the defendant no, 2 being plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 22 of 1982 against the plaintiff challenging the plaintiffs settlement and the eviction notice as illegal, without jurisdiction and void and the suit was decreed on contest on 31.8.83.. The defendant nos. 2 and 3 purchased 20 decimals, of .land from defendant No. 1 and have been residing there by constructing houses. The Assistant Custodian of Enemy. Property by order dated 20.1.83 released 20 decimals of suit land from the list of enemy property:17 decimal of suit Land which the .plaintiff alleged that Jahura Bibi is in rightful possession has been released by the Additional Deputy Commissioner . (Revenue) .and Assistant Custodian by order dated 5.4.83 from the list of -enemy property and as such the lease of entire .39 decimals of land stand ceased automatically by operation of law and that the defendant no.. 1 has obtained the right, title and interest in the suit land and the plaintiff deed not have any subsisting right on-the basis of lease from the enemy property authority and he has-no cause of action for the suit and the plaintiff having failed to institute the suit for declaration against the ex-parte decree dated 8.7.77 in Title Suit No. 70 of 1974, the same is barred by limitation and the suit is not maintainable. In Miscellaneous Case No. 173 of 1977 at the instance of the plaintiff, the Court observed as under -

"Plaintiff Johura Bibi filed the original suit (T.S. No. 70/1974) challenging the order of the lease "of the Custodian alleging her settlement from original Land lords. Subsequently there was. .Rent Suit (No. 22/1957) and there was title suit by the plaintiff  OP and got the decree for the said land and he said documents were exhibited in the original suit. So under these circumstances the order of the enemy is liable to be set aside: So the petitioner is trying to harass: the plaintiff-O.P. by filing so many petitions.

And as such the plaintiff instead of instituting a suit within a period of 3 years for declaration of title has instituted the present suit after a lapse of 5 years and the same is apparently time barred. The plaintiffs suit also does not have any cause of action and the plaintiff is continuing with instituting the suits in order to harass the defendant no.1 having no cause of action for the suits and as such prayed for rejection of the plaint.

4. The learned Munsif by order dated 12.9.84 rejected the plaint. On appeal in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 139 of 1984 at the instance of the defendants, the same was allowed by judgment and order dated 6.4.86 setting aside the judgment and order of the learned Munsif. Thereafter, the defendants moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

5. Mr. Md. Nurul Huq, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioners submits that from the averments made in the plaint itself as regard the Title Suit No. 145 of 1951, Title Suit No. 70 of 1974 and the Rent Case No. 22 of 1957 being barred by limitation, the plaint was liable to be rejected as the same is barred by law in view of Article 120 of the Limitation Act read with Section 3 of the said Act The learned Counsel further submits with reference to Exhibits—B and B( 1) to the application that the suit land has been released from the list of enemy property. The plaintiff though claimed himself to be the lessee, there is no existing right of the plaintiff as a lessee in respect of the suit land as the enemy property authority has already released the suit land in favour of its owners and as such the suit is hit by the provision of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiff having no title has no right to sue for which the plaint is liable to be rejected. The learned Counsel further submits that in view of the fact that the plaintiff has no subsisting interest in the subject-matter, the suit is not maintainable under the provision of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiff has no legal character or legal right on his being ceasing to be a lessee.

6. Mr. A.Y. Masihuzzaman, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs opposite party no. 1 submits that in view of the scope of Order 7, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Court is to confine itself within the plaint and not the written statement. The learned Counsel further submits that the plaintiff having asserted his title in the suit land on the basis of his purchase from Sailabala in respect of half of the suit land and the remaining half as a lessee under the enemy property authority and prayed for declaration that the suit land is an enemy property, the plaint is not liable to be rejected as the said claim is not barred under any law. The learned Counsel next submits that in view of the prayer in respect of Title Suit No. 145 of 1951 on the allegation of fraudulent suppression of summons and the declaration in respect of the ex-parte decree of Title Suit No. 70 of 1974 and the decree in Rent Case No. 22 of 1957 are not barred. The matter is to be decided on evidence and at least under Order 14, Rule 1 of the Code instead of throwing the plaint under Order 7, Rule 11 of the Code.

7. It appears from the plaint that the plaintiff himself has admitted Title Suit No. 70 of 1974 to be barred by limitation as the suit was filed on 5.4.83 in respect of an ex-parte decree dated 1.3.77 for which he filed the miscellaneous case under Order 9, R.:21e 13 of the Code and became unsuccessful. The plaintiff has alleged fraudulent suppression of summons and notices in Title Suit No. 145 of 1951 but has simply alleged obtaining of sole-decree in Rent Suit No. 22 of 1957. Apparently, Title Suit No. 70 of 1974 being baby limitation and as to whether the Title Suit No. 145 of 1951 or for that matter declaration regarding Rent Suit No. 22 of 1957 are barred by limitation or not could be decided by framing an issue under the provision of Order 14. Rule I of the Code. The submission of the learned Counsel for the petitioner that the plaint has to be read meaningfully so as to avoid any meritless plaint in the sense of not disclosing any cause of action is difficult to sustain in view of the assertion in the plaint that the plaintiff purchased the interest of the admitted owner Sailabala by registered deed or alternatively on the basis of his being a lessee in possession on payment of rent by Laking lease from the enemy property authority and as such the decision in the case of Fatima Moeen-vs-Addi. District Judge, Sheikhupura and ors, reported in S.C.M.R. (1992), 1199 is of no avail to the petitioners as at least in respect of Title Suit No. 145 of 1951 fraud has been alleged for which the suit would not be apparently said to be time barred.

8. It is now well-settled principle of law that in exercise of the power of rejecting a plaint the Court can look into the statements of the plaint only and it cannot consider any fact stated in the written statement or the application under Order 7, Rule 11 of the Code or any document produced by the defendant (35 DLR, 217, 41 DLR 77, 43 DLR 327). At this initial stage of the instant suit it is the plaint of the suit which is the only record before the Court and it is on the basis of that plaint that the Court be low is to see whether the suit is barred by any law or whether it is not otherwise maintainable. This is the view which has been taken in the case of Kazi Mobarrak Ali-Vs-Mohammad Yeasin Mazumder and ors. reported in 43 D.L.R. (AD.) 60. The said view has been consistently followed by this .Court. In a suit barred by limitation it must appear to be so but atleast in respect of Title Suit No. 145 of 1951 and the averment made in the plaint as because fraud has been alleged the suit does not apparently appear to be barred which may be considered by framing an issue Under Order 14, Rule 1 of the Code to see as to whether the suit is maintainable on the ground that the suit is barred by limitation. Though Mr. Nurul Huq, learned Counsel for the petitioner has referred to the decision in the cases reported in A.I.R. 1917 and 1918 that when the plaintiffs right as a lessee ceased to exist, the suit barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case Barring the statements made in the application under Order 7, Rule 11 of the Code. From the statement of the plaint itself it does not show that the right to sue has ceased to exist in respect of a lessee for declaration that the suit property is an enemy property. In that view of the matter, the decision reported in B.C.R. 1984 (Dhaka), 264 referred to by Mr. Huq has also no manner of application. However, in view of the assertion in the application under Order 7, Rule 11 of the Code that the property has been released by the enemy property authority in favour of its owner whereby the plaintiff has ceased to be a lessee and thereby no right to sue exists in him so as to bar the suit under the provision of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act or that the declaration as sought for in respect of Title Suit No. 145 of 1951 and Title Suit No. 70 of 1974 are barred by limitation or not can be decided by framing a preliminary issue in the suit.

<u>9. It appears that the learned Court of appeal below has concentrated much on the cause of action on consideration of the averments regarding Title Suit No. 70 of 1974 but has not considered the statements made in respect of Title Suit No. 145 of 1951, in as much as, from the statements made in the plaint the said suit does not appear to be barred by limitation. Any observation/finding of this Court made herein shall have no effect on the court below while deciding any issue either under Order 14, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure or at the hearing of the suit.</u>

<u>10. It appears that the learned Munsif has passed the order by rejecting the plaint by a mute order in exercise of his judicial discretion but in view of the fact that he has been exercising his discretion by which he ought to have assigned reasons, so as to enable the litigant public and the superior Courts to see as to how he has exercised his judicial mind in disposing of the judicial discretion. This Court is of the view that in future the learned Munsif shall not exercise his judicial discretion by any mute or non-speaking order or in a slip-shod manner.</u>

11. In view of the finding above, the judgment of the trial Court is not sustainable in law and as such the impugned judgment and decree are maintained. There is no error of law occasioning failure of justice in the impugned judgment.

12. In the result, the Rule is discharged without, however, any order as to costs.

End.

case_source: Arising out of the judgment and order dated 31.12.86 passed by the Munsif, 4th Court Dhaka, in Misc. Case No79 of 1985 arising out of T.S. No.4 16 of 1985
full_judgment:
D.M. Ansaruddin Ahmed, J: This Rule issued on an application under Section 115 of the bode of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff is directed against the, judgment and order passed on 31.12.1986 by the Munsif, 4th Court, Dhaka allowing Mis. Case No.79 of 1985 under Order 9 Rule of the Code using out of Title Suit No.416 of 1985 (originally Title Suit No. 327 of 1981 of the local Munsif's 6th court).

2. The above mentioned suit was instituted by the plaintiff (petitioner herein) against 5 defendants, that is, 4 brothers and 1 brother's wife for their ejectment as licensees from the suit premises which constitute the eastern, part measuring about 2 Kathas of land with structure thereon out of holding No. 213, West Bashabo, Dhaka. The 4 brothers filed a joint written statement and the 5th defendant filed a separate written statement in the suit. Subsequently on the death on defendant No. 4 his heirs including some minors were brought on record on 23.2.1983. Ultimately the court guardian submitted his report on 5.1.1985. On this day the plaintiff filed hazira but the defendants were absent and the suit was fixed for ex-parte hearing on 28.1.1985. On the date fixed the suit was transferred to the local 4th Court of Munsif in pursuance of an earlier order of the District Judge. The transferee court, after 2 or 3 suo motu adjournments, decreed the suit ex-parte on 23.3.1985. Subsequently the plaintiff got the plaint schedule and the decree amended by inserting the description of the suit holding under an order dated 18.5.1985. Thereafter, on 1.6.1985, defendant No.1 Abdul Kader, defendant No.3 Ashraf Mia and defendant No.4 (kha) Bacchu Mia filed the Misc. Case No.79 of 1985 under Order 9 Rule 13 for setting aside the ex-parte decree taking the plea that after transfer of the suit from the original court they were not informed about the proceeding. The plaintiff contested the rehearing case by filing a written objection and at the heating only 1 witness was examined on the either side. The learned Munsif has decided the point on limitation to favour of the petitioners for the reason that they filed Misc. Case within a period of 30 days from date of amendment of the decree. On the point as to whether the petitioners were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing in the suit the learned Munsif has also decided it in the affirmative believing the petitioners case that they were not informed about the transfer of the suit in spite of a definite order having been passed in the order sheet by the transferee court and that they had no knowledge of the progress of the proceedings in the transferee court. Me has also believed the petitioners contention that they for the first time learnt about the ex-parte decree when the plaintiff made an attempt to take possession of the premises through court on 16.6.1985. The learned Munsif has accordingly allowed the Misc. Case subject however to condition of deposit by the defendants petitioners of an amount of Tk. 1,000/- as cost to the credit of the plaintiff opposite party by 30.1.1987 and the order sheet shows that the amount was duly deposited. It is against this order that the plaintiff has obtained the instant Rule.

3. It has been urged by Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur, the learned Advocate for petitioner, that the learned court below has fallen into errors in allowing the Misc. Case. He submits that the Misc. Case has been disposed of without bringing on record the heirs of defendant No.1 Abdul Kader who was petitioner No.2 in the Misc. Case and died on 4.6.1986. He further submits that defendant No.2 and some of the substituted heirs of defendant No. 4 were not parties in the rehearing case and as such the case was bad for defect of parties and in any view, the decree against the defendants not parties in the re-hearing case could not be set aside.

Mr. Gafur further submits that it was the defendants duty to keep track of the course of the proceedings and as such there was no sufficient cause for their ignorance of the date of the decree and for non-appearance on the date. Mr. Sultan Ahmad, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties, supports the impugned judgment and order and submits that the decree being joint and indivisible, any one of the defendants could very well maintain the re-hearing application for getting the ex-parte decree as a whole set aside, without the other defendants on record. On the question of limitation, his reply is that not only the learned Judge at the time of admission of the Misc. Case condoned the delay on the specific prayer of the applicants but also the decree having been amended within the period of limitation, there was no question of any such bar being involved. His further submission is that the court below has rightly considered the fact that having not been informed about the transfer of the suit the defendants were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing therein.

4. In the suit the defendants filed written statements and subsequently on the death of one of the defendants the plaintiff brought his heirs on record. A period of about 2 years was taken for service of process upon the heirs and for submission of the court guardian's report. The last date for submission of the court when the guardian submitted his report on 5.1.1985 guardian's report was 5.1.1985, the suit was fixed for ex-parte hearing depriving the defendants an opportunity to contest the suit. Since then the orders had always been passed for ex-parte disposal of the suit and as such the defendants had no opportunity to enter appearance. In addition when the suit was transferred to another court the transferee court on receipt of the record passed an order aught a few days directing the office to inform the parties but this order was not complied with. It is true that under ordinary circumstances the parties are required to keep track of the course of the proceedings. But when the court guardian submitted his report it was the duty of the court to fix a date for the parties to take steps, if any, or for framing of issue (the defendants having already filed written statements). Instead, the date was fixed for ex-parte hearing thus shutting the door on the face of the defendants for no fault of theirs. Again, while disposing of the suit ex-parte, the court failed to see if its order for informing the parties about the transfer of the suit was duly complied with and the defendants had knowledge about the pendency of the proceedings in that court. In my view, therefore, the learned Munsif has very rightly held that the applicants were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for heating.

5. It will appear that while praying for setting aside the decree the defendants also made a prayer under Section 5 of the limitation Act for condonation of the delay. This fact is very much specifically mentioned in the order whereby the learned Munsif, after hearing the, defendant's learned Advocate, registered the case and directed issue of process upon the opposite parties. This is a clear evidence of the court below having condoned the delay by implication. Moreover, there is another question which has been considered by the court below. Subsequent to the passing of the ex-parte decree the plaintiff prayed for amendment of the plaint and consequential amendment in the decree also. The prayer was allowed on 18.5.1985 and the plaint as well as the decree were accordingly amended. Since them defendants could not get set aside the original decree without the amendment, they are, while praying for setting it aside, entitled to compute the period of limitation from the date of the amendment. In such view of the matter the learned Munsif has rightly held that the i.e. hearing case having been filed within 30 days therefrom is not barred by limitation.

<u>6. There is no dispute however that the defendants No.1 who was one of the applicants. in the re-hearing case died on 4.6.1986 that is during the pendency of the case. His heirs were not substituted. There is nothing on record to show as to who were his heirs or anybody other than those on record was his heir. Whatever they may be, it is to be seen whether in absence of defendant No.1 or defendant No.2 of the remaining heirs of V the defendant No. 4 in the rehearing proceedings the decree could be set aside as a whole.</u>

<u>The provisio to Rule 13 of Order 9 CPC runs as follows. Where the decree is of such a nature that it cannot be set aside as against such defendant only it may be set aside as against all or any of the other defendant also.</u>

<u>Rule 13 thus recognises circumstances under which an ex-parte decree can be set aside as a whole even if some of the defendants do not apply for it. In view of the proviso, ordinarily an ex-parte decree should not be set aside against those who do not apply. The exceptional case contemplated by the proviso may include a case where the decree is joint and indivisible. The instant decree for recovery of possession of a house in the joint possession of the defendants is such an instance. Here the decree is joint and the liabilities of the defendants, all brothers and one of the brother's wife, are not separate. In such circumstances the decree could, at the instance of one of the defendants, properly be set aside as against other defendants as well. It may be further pointed out that for setting aside an ex-party decree, none but the plaintiff; in whose favour the decree stands, needs be notified. Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur apprehends that for no fault of his he may be faced with serious objection from the other side in the court below when be will apply for bringing on record the heirs of the deceased defendants. The apprehension seems to be unfounded simply for the reason that the Misc. Proceeding was not started by him and he was not required to bring the deceased's representatives on record within the prescribed period. Burden of substitution in a proceeding lies on the initiator of the said proceeding and not upon the opposite side.</u>

7. In view of what has been discussed above, I must hold that the learned Judge has in setting aside the ex-parte decree not committed any error of law. In the facts an circumstances of the case, the impugned judgment and order is well justified and as such it is not liable to be interfered with in revision.

In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

Sent down the lower court records at once.

End.

caseno: Civil Revision No. 3380 of 1993 with Civil Revision No. 3381 of 1983.
lawyer:
Fida M Kamal with Idris Khan, Advocates—For the Petitioner. 
TH Khan with SK Zulfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury, Advocates—For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Ambia Khatun ------ Petitioner 
Vs
Abdus Salam & others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
These two Rules by defendant-respondent-petitioner directed against a single judgment dated 18-8-1993 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Chittagong, in Other Appeal No. 244 of 1988 and in other Appeal No. 245 of 1988, allowing with the appeal heard analogously, thereby dismissing the suits on reversing the judgment and decree dated 28-4-1988 passed to the then learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Chittagong in Partition Suit No.63 of 1970 and other Suit No.7 of 1972 heard analogously, as such, this judgment would govern both the Rules.

2. The opposite parties as plaintiffs, praying for a saham in the suit property, filed Partition Suit No.63 of 1970. The petitioner as plaintiff prayed for ejectment of monthly tenant filed Other Suit No.7 of 1972. Money Suit No.13 of 1972 was also heard analogously with these suits.

3. The plaint case of Partition Suit No.63 of 1970 is that Abdur Rahman Sowdagar, son of Ebadullah Sowdagar took settlement of the suit land on 15-7-57 from late SK Rafiuddin Siddique. Abdur Rahman Sowdagar alone possessed the suit land by constructing houses. Ebadullah Sowdagar died leaving two sons, Abdur Rahman Sowdagar and Abdul Jalil Sowdagar Abdur Rahman died leaving two wives, plaintiff No.1, and defendant No.1 and 3 nephews in plaintiff Nos. 2 to 4. Plaintiff No. 1 got 2 annas share out of the suit land and also defendant No.1 got two annas share. Plaintiffs Nos. 2 to 4 got 12 annas share. Thus in total, all the plaintiffs got 14 annas share of the suit property. The lands of RS Plot Nos. 321 is possessed by the plaintiffs, Nurul Islam and Abdul Mabud were the bharatias of the plaintiffs. In the house of RS Plot No. 322, there are 4 rooms, plaintiff No. 4 used to possess two rooms. In other two rooms defendant No. 5 took possession on the plea that defendant No.1 will get the same. Defendants are possessing more rooms than that of their shares. Defendant No.2 is brother of defendant No.1. Defendants created some spurious documents to deprive the plaintiffs from enjoying their share. Defendant No.1 will get her share only by right of inheritance. The deeds of defendants are void, illegal and without consideration. On these pleadings, plaintiffs demanded partition of the suit property but the defendants refused. Hence the suit.

4. Defendant No.5 contested the suit and his case is that the suit land originally belonged to Surendra; Md Rafiuddin got the land from Surendra on 22-5-16. Rafiuddin paid rents to the landlord and taxes to the Municipality. It is the further case of this defendant that Surendra became malik dokhalker by way of purchase on 1-9-20. Rafiuddin and Surendra took 'namjaree' settlement and Rafiuddin acquired projayee satta' on 7-9-21. The name of Menatosh was recorded in RS Khatian as bondobesti right; he exclusively possessed the suit land. Abdur Rahman gave lease of the suit land to his wife, Samana Kha tun and he handed over possession to her on 19-3-57 and thereafter, Abdur Rahman died, Samana Khatoon became owner of the suit land having title and possession. Abdur Rahman had no right in the suit land and Samana Khatoon had right and possession over the suit land exclusively since 1949. Thereafter, Samana sold the suit land to Abdul Huq on 15-3-69. Her husband, Abdur Rahman used to look after the affairs of the suit property and plaintiffs did not demand any partition and are not entitled to have any portion of land of the suit property. This suit has been filed fraudulently and this defendant is entitled to realise rents from tenants of RS Plot Nos. 321 and 322 and on these pleadings, this defendant prayed for dismissal of the suit.

5. Defendant No.3, who is plaintiff of Money Suit No.13 of 1972, appeared in the suit and took several times but ultimately did not contest the suit.

6. On the pleadings of the parties, the learned Subordinate Judges framed five issues i.e. issue No.1 for maintainability of the suit; issue No.2 relating to whether the plaintiffs are entitled to the saham as prayed for and to what extent; issue No.3 relating to defect of parties; issue No.4 relating to whether all the lands of the parties have been brought into hotchpotch, and issue No.5 relating to what relief, if any, the plaintiff are entitled to.

7. Learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the evidence on record, by judgment and decree dated 28-4-1988 dismissed Partition Suit No.63 of 1970 against defendant No.3 with costs. Other Suit No.7 of 1972 was decreed. The learned Subordinate Judge ordered that the plaintiff of this suit by evicting the defendants from the suit premises would get khas possession of the same and directed for recovery of Taka 140 from the defendants and for payment of Taka 10 per day from 1-9-1970 till 28-4-1988. The learned Subordinate Judge dismissed Money Suit No.13 of 1972.

8. Against this judgment, the plaintiff preferred two appeals. Title Appeal No.244 of 1988 was preferred against the judgment of Partition Suit No.63 of 1970 and Title Appeal No. 245 of 1988 was preferred against the judgment of other Suit No.7 of 1972, These two appeals, on transfer, were heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Chittagong who, by the impugned judgment, allowed both the appeals, Against the judgment passed in Other Appeal No.244 of 1988 Rule is obtained in CR No. 3381 of 1993 and against Judgment passed in other Appeal No. 245 of 1988, Rule is obtained in CR No.3380 of 1993.

9. Mr Fida M Kamal, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioner, submits that judgment of the Court of appeal below is not a proper judgment of reversal. He further submits that the Court of appeal below misconstrued and misinterpreted the material evidences, particularly wasiatnama dated 19-34957, Exhibit H and thereby fallen into error of law in decreeing Partition Suit No. 63 of 1970. He further submits that the Court of Appeal below fails to consider that defendant No.1 acquired good title through wasiatnama dated 19-3-57. Learned Counsel further submits that the Court of Appeal below fails to read properly Exhibit-G, the patta and on misconstruction of Exhibits-G and H, that is patta and wasiatnama, wrongly held that defendant did not acquire any title over the suit land through these two deeds.

10. On the other hand, Mr TH Khan, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party, submits that the Court of appeal below committed no illegality in disbelieving Exhibits G and H. He elaborately submits that Exhibit. H, which is wasiatnama, is to be construed strictly. Wasiatnama contains certain statements which rendered itself to be void and this wasiatnama, being a void document need not to be declared as an illegal document. He further submits that Exhibit G is patta which being unilateral document by which no title was passed. He further submits that on the basis of Exhibit H. which is a void document, Samana Khatoon sold the land to her brother, Abdul Huq and 5 gondas of land on 23-12-69 to Ambia Khatoon, Exhibit F(1), and this Ambia Khatoon, who is defendant No.5 in the partition suit, as such, he submits, that when wasiatnama itself being a void document, no title was passed from Samena Khatoon, who is recipient of this wasiatnama, to Abdul Huq and to that effect to Ambia Khatoon, purchaser from Abdul Huq and, on the basis of such purchase, Ambia Khatoon filed Other Suit No.7 of 1972 for ejecting Abdus Salam as her tenant, who is one of the plaintiffs of the partition Suit No.63 of 1970, as such, Ambia Khatun being a title less person, she acquired no title by purchase from Abdul Huq, to evict Abdus Salam from the suit land.

11. On the submission of the parties I am now to consider specially Exhibits G and H. If it is found that Exhibits G and H are not valid documents of title then it would be held that defendant No.1, i.e. plaintiff of Other Suit No.7 of 1972 have no authority, either to acquire any excess land than 2 annas share by inheritance or acquired no title to evict Abdus Salam from the suit land and Court of appeal below committed no illegality in decreeing Partition Suit No.63 of 1970 and dismissing other suit No.7 of 1972.

12. From a reading of Exhibit H, I find it starts with এই অছিয়ত নামা আমার মৃত্যুর পূর্বে বলবৎ হইবে which is totally contradictory to the meaning of wasiatnama. Wasiatnama generally and legally takes effect after the demise of the propositus but Exhibit-H speaks otherwise i.e. it would take effect during the lifetime of propositus rendering the same to be a void document. I find in this wasiatnama, a schedule was given by which the recipients of this wasiatnama was given 16 decimals equivalent to 8 gondas of land. Wasiatnama, as I have already found, legally takes effect after the death of the propositus, not before his death. In spite of that, let me consider, by this wasiatnama, what the propositus intends to wish. Since by this wasiatnama certain lands have been given to the recipients by Samena Khatoon, who is the wife of the donor, Abdur Rahman Sowdagar, as such, each and every stanza of this Exhibit H is to be considered strictly. In this wasiatnama it is further written that;

“আমি ইতিপূর্বে এত অছিয়ত নামা মূলে কতক সম্পত্তি আমার মৃত্যুর পর অছিয়ত নামা প্রহিতার জীবিকা নির্বাহ ও ভরন পোষনের জন্য দিয়াছি উক্ত সম্পত্তি দ্বারা আপনার জীবিকা নির্বাহ সুন্দর রুপে হইবে না অসুবিধা হওয়ার আমি পুন দ্বিতীয় অছিয়ত করিতেছি যে নিম্ন অর্থাৎ আমার মৃত্যুর পর আপনার ভরন পোষণের জন্য নির্ধারিত করা হইল। আমার মুত্যুর পর উক্ত সম্পত্তি আপনার নিজ নামে ও স্বত্ত দখল নিয়া উক্ত সম্পত্তির উপস্বত্ব দ্বারা আপনার ভরন পোষন ইত্যাদি জীবিকা নির্বাহ করিতে পারিবেন।

<u>13. These statements are self-contradictory as the recital of the wasiatnama speaks otherwise. Moreover, I find from this wasiatnama that earlier also, propositus made a wasiatnama by which he has already made some arrangement of his properties. Then why this wasiatnama? This is probably to make arrangement of the properties in a way to satisfy the recipient, who is none else than the wife of the propositus in preference to all other heirs who were given properties by the earlier wasiatnama. Since this wasiatnama contains some conditions not in according with law, it is hit by the provisions of Mohammedan Law and stands as a void document and void document needs no declaration to that effect.</u>

<u>The appellate Court held that through Exhibit-H no transfer was made. I concur with this view. Other document of title of defendant No.1 is patta, Exhibit G. This Exhibit G was made in 1949. By this Exhibit G, defendant wanted to prove that Abdur Rahman Sowdagar settled some properties with defendant No.1 in 1949. But it appears that Abdur Rahman got settlement of the land mentioned in Exhibit G from Rafiuddin on 15-7-57. If Abdur Rahman got the land in 1957 then how he could settled the said land in favour of defendant No.1 by Exhibit G in 1949. This is also against the settle principle of law that before acquiring title one cannot settle the land to another and if he settle such land, then it also stands as void. Defendant No.1 could make out a case under section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act, i.e feeding of title by estoppel but defendant No. 1 did not do so. The argument was forwarded from the side of defendant-petitioner that name of defendant No.1 has been recorded in RS Khatian in 1960 but recording the name of defendant No.1 is not on the strength of Exhibit-G or H, but on the strength of her inheritance i.e. defendant No.1 is legally entitled to two annas share from Abdur Rahman Sowdagar and her name is recorded to that effect. On consideration of Exhibits G and H, I find that these are not documents of title and, as such, if these two deeds are left aside from consideration, then defendant No.1 would get only 2 annas share as heir as wife of Abdur Rahman and in the suit property. In partition Suit, plaintiffs and defendants stand on equal footing and no weakness of plaintiffs or defendants, ipso facto, give saham to anyone. The defendant No.1 is to prove acquisition of property through Exhibits G and H to have partition of the suit land to the extent of 14 annas share in the suit property. In that view of the matter, I find that the learned Additional District Judge committed no illegality in decreeing partition Suit to the extent of 14 annas share. I also hold that since plaintiff of Other Suit No.7 of 1972 acquired no title by purchase as her vendor acquired no title by wasiatnama and patta, the suit i.e. Other Suit No.7 of 1972, filed by Ambia Khatoon for ejectment of Abdus Salam, who is a plaintiff in Partition Suit No. 63 of 1970, has been rightly dismissed. In that view of the matter, I find no substance in this Rule.</u>

14. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

Send down the lower Court records.

End.
